title.zh: 卷六十二 南唐世家第二: 李昪
title.en: Volume 62: Hereditary House of Southern Tang
title.raw: 卷六十二 南唐世家第二: 李昪 Volume 62: Hereditary House of Southern Tang

sentences.zh: 李昪，字正倫，徐州人也。

translations.literal: Li Bian, courtesy name Zhenglun, was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bian, whose courtesy name was Zhenglun, came from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世本微賤，父榮，遇唐末之亂，不知其所終。

translations.literal: His family had long been of humble rank; his father Rong, encountering the chaos at the end of Tang, met an end unknown.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been of low station. His father Rong disappeared in the turmoil at the end of the Tang, and no one knew what became of him.

sentences.zh: 昪少孤，流寓濠、泗間，楊行密攻濠州，得之，奇其狀貌，養以為子。

translations.literal: Bian was orphaned young and drifted between Hao and Si; Yang Xingmi attacked Hao Prefecture, obtained him, marveled at his appearance, and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, Bian wandered between the Hao and Si regions. When Yang Xingmi took Hao Prefecture he came into Yang's hands; struck by the boy's looks, Yang adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 而楊氏諸子不能容，行密以乞徐溫，乃冒姓徐氏，名知誥。

translations.literal: But the sons of the Yang clan could not tolerate him; Xingmi gave him to Xu Wen, whereupon he falsely took the surname Xu and the name Zhihao.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang sons would not accept him, so Xingmi handed him over to Xu Wen. He then took the Xu surname and the name Zhihao.

sentences.zh: 及壯，身長七尺，廣顙隆準。

translations.literal: When grown, his body was seven chi in height, with a broad forehead and a high nose bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In manhood he stood seven chi tall, with a broad forehead and prominent nose.

sentences.zh: 為人溫厚有謀。

translations.literal: As a man he was mild and substantial and possessed stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and steady by nature, yet shrewd.

sentences.zh: 為吳樓船軍使，以舟兵屯金陵。

translations.literal: He served as Wu's tower-ship military commissioner, stationing naval troops at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He became commissioner of Wu's tower-ship forces and kept the fleet at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 柴再用攻宣州，用其兵殺李遇，以功拜升州刺史。

translations.literal: Chai Zaiyong attacked Xuan Prefecture; using his troops he killed Li Yu, and for merit was appointed prefect of Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Chai Zaiyong campaigned against Xuan Prefecture, Bian's troops killed Li Yu. For this service he was made prefect of Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 時江淮初定，州、縣吏多武夫，務賦斂為戰守，獨好學，接禮儒者，能自勵為勤儉，以寬仁為政，民稍譽之。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiang-Huai region had just been pacified; prefectural and county officials were mostly military men who strove in tax levies for war and defense. He alone loved learning, received and honored Confucians, could urge himself to diligence and frugality, and took lenience and benevolence as his government; the people gradually praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangtze had only just been pacified, and most local officials were soldiers bent on taxing the people to fund war. He alone favored learning, treated scholars with courtesy, practiced thrift, and governed with clemency, and the people began to speak well of him.

sentences.zh: 徐溫鎮潤州，以升、池等六州為屬，溫聞理升州有善政，往視之，見其府庫充實，城壁修整，乃徙治之，而遷潤州刺史。

translations.literal: Xu Wen held Run Prefecture and made Sheng, Chi, and five other prefectures subordinate. Wen heard that governing Sheng had good administration, went to inspect it, saw its treasuries full and its walls repaired, then moved his seat of rule there and transferred the prefect of Run.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen was stationed at Runzhou with six prefectures including Sheng and Chi under him. Hearing of Bian's good rule at Shengzhou, Wen went to see for himself, found the treasury full and the defenses in order, moved his base there, and sent Bian to Runzhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 初不欲往，屢求宣州，溫不與。

translations.literal: At first he did not wish to go and repeatedly requested Xuan Prefecture; Wen did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He was reluctant to leave at first and asked repeatedly for Xuanzhou, but Wen refused.

sentences.zh: 既而徐知訓為朱瑾所殺，溫居金陵，未及聞。

translations.literal: Before long Xu Zhixun was killed by Zhu Jin; Wen resided at Jinling and had not yet heard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xu Zhixun was killed by Zhu Jin. Xu Wen was at Jinling and had not yet learned of it.

sentences.zh: 居潤州，近廣陵，得先聞，即日以州兵渡江定亂，遂得政。

translations.literal: Residing at Run Prefecture, near Guangling, he heard first, that very day led prefectural troops across the river to settle the disorder, and thereby obtained power.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was at Runzhou, close to Guangling, and heard the news first. He crossed the river the same day with his troops, put down the disturbance, and seized control of the government.

sentences.zh: 昪事徐溫甚孝謹，溫嘗罵其諸子不如昪，諸子頗不能容，而知訓尤甚，嘗召昪飲酒，伏劍士欲害之，行酒吏刁彥能覺之，酒至，以手爪掐之，悟起走，乃免。

translations.literal: Bian served Xu Wen with great filial piety and care. Wen once scolded his sons, saying they were not equal to Bian; the sons could scarcely tolerate this, and Zhixun especially so. He once summoned Bian to drink wine and hid swordsmen to harm him. The wine-server Diao Yanneng perceived it; when the wine arrived he pinched Bian with his fingernails, Bian understood, rose and fled, and thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Bian served Xu Wen with devoted respect. Wen once berated his own sons for falling short of Bian, which the sons resented, Zhixun most of all. Zhixun once invited Bian to drink and hid swordsmen to kill him. The cupbearer Diao Yanneng noticed the plot and, when he brought the wine, dug his nails into Bian's flesh. Bian understood, sprang up, and fled, and so survived.

sentences.zh: 後自潤州入覲，知訓與飲於山光寺，又欲害之，徐知諫以其謀告，起遁去。

translations.literal: Later, coming from Run Prefecture to attend audience, Zhixun drank with him at Shanguang Temple and again wished to harm him. Xu Zhijian reported his plot, and Bian rose and slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Bian came from Runzhou to pay his respects, Zhixun drank with him at Shanguang Temple and again tried to kill him. Xu Zhijian warned him of the scheme, and Bian fled.

sentences.zh: 知訓以劍授刁彥能，使追殺之，及於中途而還，紿以不及，由是得免。

translations.literal: Zhixun gave a sword to Diao Yanneng and sent him to pursue and kill him. Reaching midway he returned and deceived him, saying he had not caught up; thereby Bian escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun handed a sword to Diao Yanneng and ordered him to run Bian down. Diao turned back halfway and lied that he had not caught him, and Bian was spared again.

sentences.zh: 後貴，以彥能為撫州節度使。

translations.literal: Later, when he had become eminent, he made Yanneng military governor of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Bian rose to power, he appointed Yanneng military governor of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 知訓之用事也，嘗淩弱楊氏而驕侮諸將，遂以見殺。

translations.literal: When Zhixun held power he had bullied the Yang clan and arrogantly insulted the generals, and thereby met death.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhixun held power he had bullied the Yang house and treated the generals with contempt, which led to his assassination.

sentences.zh: 及昪秉政，欲收人心，乃寬刑法、推恩信，起延賓亭以待四方之士，引宋齊丘、駱知祥、王令謀等為謀客，士有羈旅於吳者，皆齒用之。

translations.literal: When Bian held government he wished to win people's hearts, and therefore eased penal law and extended favor and trust. He built the Pavilion for Extending Guests to await men from the four quarters, brought in Song Qiqiu, Luo Zhixiang, Wang Lingmou, and others as strategists, and for scholars sojourning in Wu he employed them all in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bian held power he sought to win hearts by lightening punishments and showing generosity. He built the Pavilion for Honored Guests to receive scholars from afar, took Song Qiqiu, Luo Zhixiang, Wang Lingmou, and others as advisers, and gave posts in turn to every learned man who came to Wu as a guest.

sentences.zh: 嘗陰使人察視民間有婚喪匱乏者，往往赒給之。

translations.literal: He once secretly sent men to observe among the people those with weddings or funerals who lacked means, and often gave them relief.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had agents watch for families in need at weddings or funerals and often sent them aid.

sentences.zh: 盛暑未嘗張蓋、操扇，左右進蓋，必卻之，曰：「士眾尚多暴露，我何用此？

translations.literal: In the height of summer he never spread a canopy or wielded a fan. When attendants offered a canopy he always refused it, saying: "The soldiers and masses still stand much in the open—what use have I for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Even in fierce summer heat he never used a canopy or fan. When attendants offered a canopy he always waved it away, saying, "My troops are still out in the sun—why should I use this?"

sentences.zh: 」以故溫雖遙秉大政，而吳人頗已歸。

translations.literal: " For this reason, although Wen still held great government from afar, the people of Wu had already largely submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Because of such conduct, the people of Wu were already turning to Bian even though Xu Wen still held supreme authority from a distance.

sentences.zh: 昪照鑒見白須，顧其吏周宗嘆曰：「功業已就，而吾老矣，奈何？

translations.literal: Bian looked in a mirror and saw white whiskers. Turning to his officer Zhou Zong he sighed: "The achievement is already done, yet I am old—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Bian looked in a mirror, saw white in his beard, and sighed to his officer Zhou Zong, "My work is done, but I am old—what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 」宗知其意，馳詣廣陵見宋齊丘，謀禪代。

translations.literal: " Zong knew his intent, galloped to Guangling to see Song Qiqiu, and plotted the transfer of the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " Zong understood his meaning, rode in haste to Guangling to see Song Qiqiu, and laid plans for the abdication.

sentences.zh: 齊丘以為未可，請斬宗以謝吳人，黜宗為池州刺史。

translations.literal: Qiqiu thought it not yet possible and requested that Zong be beheaded to appease the people of Wu; Zong was demoted to prefect of Chi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu judged the time not ripe and urged that Zong be executed to placate Wu opinion. Zong was instead demoted to prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 吳臨江王濛者，怨徐氏舍己而立溥，心嘗不平，及將謀篡國，先廢濛為歷陽公，使吏以兵守之。

translations.literal: Wu Prince of Linjiang Meng resented the Xu clan for setting him aside and enthroning Pu; his heart had long been uneasy. When Bian was about to plot usurpation of the state, he first deposed Meng as Duke of Liyang and sent officials with troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Prince of Linjiang, Yang Meng, resented the Xu clan for passing him over in favor of Yang Pu and had long nursed a grievance. Before seizing the throne, Bian first degraded Meng to Duke of Liyang and set officials with troops to watch him.

sentences.zh: 濛殺守者，奔廬州節度使周本。

translations.literal: Meng killed the guards and fled to Zhou Ben, military governor of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng killed his guards and fled to Zhou Ben, military governor of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 本，吳舊將也，聞濛至，欲納之，為其子祚所止。

translations.literal: Ben was an old general of Wu. Hearing Meng had arrived, he wished to receive him but was stopped by his son Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was a veteran officer of Wu. When he heard Meng had come, he meant to take him in, but his son Zuo prevented him.

sentences.zh: 本曰：「此吾故主家郎君也，何忍拒之！

translations.literal: Ben said: "This is a young lord of my former master's house—how could I bear to refuse him!"
translations.idiomatic: Ben said, "This young man is of my old master's house—how could I turn him away!"

sentences.zh: 」遽自出迎，祚閉門遮本不得出，縛濛送金陵，見殺。

translations.literal: " He was about to go out himself to welcome him when Zuo shut the gate, blocked Ben from leaving, bound Meng, and sent him to Jinling, where he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " He started to go out to welcome him himself, but Zuo barred the gate, kept Ben inside, bound Meng, sent him to Jinling, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 五年，封齊王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was created Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 已而閩、越諸國皆遣使勸進，謂人望已歸。

translations.literal: Before long the states of Min, Yue, and others all sent envoys urging his advance, saying the people's expectation had already returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the states of Min, Yue, and others sent envoys urging him to take the throne, declaring that popular sentiment was already his.

sentences.zh: 天祚三年，建齊國，置宗廟社稷，以宋齊丘、徐玠為左、右丞相。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianzuo he established the state of Qi, set up ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, and made Song Qiqiu and Xu Jie left and right chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Tianzuo era he founded the state of Qi, established ancestral temples and state altars, and appointed Song Qiqiu and Xu Jie as left and right chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 十月，溥遣攝太尉楊璘傳位於，國號齊，改元升元。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Pu sent the acting Grand Mentor Yang Lin to transmit the throne to him; the state title was Qi and the era name was changed to Shengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yang Pu sent the acting Grand Mentor Yang Lin to abdicate in his favor. The state was called Qi and the era name Shengyuan was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 以冊尊溥曰：「受禪老臣知誥，謹上冊皇帝為高尚思玄弘古讓皇帝。

translations.literal: By document he honored Pu, saying: "The old minister receiving the mandate, Zhihao, respectfully presents the document elevating the Emperor as the Lofty, Reflective, Profound, and Ancient-Emulating Abdicating Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: In the investiture text the new ruler styled himself "the old minister receiving the mandate, Zhihao," and honored Pu as the Lofty, Reflective, Profound, Ancient-Emulating Abdicating Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」追尊徐溫為忠武皇帝，封子景為吳王，封徐氏子知證江王，知諤饒王。

translations.literal: " He posthumously honored Xu Wen as Emperor Zhongwu, enfeoffed his son Jing as Prince of Wu, and enfeoffed Xu's sons Zhizheng as Prince of Jiang and Zhie as Prince of Rao.
translations.idiomatic: " He posthumously honored Xu Wen as Emperor Zhongwu, created his son Jing Prince of Wu, and enfeoffed Xu's sons Zhizheng as Prince of Jiang and Zhie as Prince of Rao.

sentences.zh: 周本與諸將至金陵勸進，歸而嘆曰：「吾不誅篡國者以報楊氏，今老矣，豈能事二姓乎！

translations.literal: Zhou Ben and the generals came to Jinling to urge his advance. Returning, he sighed: "I did not execute the usurper of the state to repay the Yang clan; now I am old—how could I serve two surnames!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ben and the other generals went to Jinling to pay homage. On his return he sighed, "I failed to kill the man who stole the realm to avenge the Yang house. I am old now—how can I serve a second master?"

sentences.zh: 」憤惋而死。

translations.literal: " He died of indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: " He died of grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，遷楊溥於潤州丹陽宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he moved Yang Pu to the Danyang Palace at Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year he moved Yang Pu to the Danyang Palace at Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 以王輿為浙西節度使、馬思讓為丹陽宮使，以嚴兵守之。

translations.literal: He made Wang Yu military governor of Zhexi and Ma Sirang keeper of the Danyang Palace, guarding him with strict troops.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wang Yu military governor of Zhexi and Ma Sirang keeper of the Danyang Palace, with a strong guard over Pu.

sentences.zh: 徐氏諸子請復姓，謙抑不敢忘徐氏恩，下其議百官，百官皆請，然後復姓李氏，改名曰。

translations.literal: The sons of the Xu clan requested restoration of his surname. With modest restraint he dared not forget Xu's kindness, submitted the matter for discussion to the hundred officials, and when all the officials requested it he then restored the surname Li and changed his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu sons asked him to resume the Li surname. He demurred, unwilling to seem ungrateful to the Xu house, and put the question to the court. When every official urged it, he took back the name Li and changed his personal name as well.

sentences.zh: 自言唐憲宗子建王恪生超，超生誌，為徐州判司；

translations.literal: He declared of himself that Prince Jian, son of Tang Xianzong, named Ke, begot Chao; Chao begot Zhi, who was an aide in the Xuzhou prefectural office;
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Prince Jian, son of Emperor Xianzong of Tang: Ke begot Chao, and Chao begot Zhi, who served as a judicial aide in Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 誌生榮。

translations.literal: Zhi begot Rong.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhi begot Rong.

sentences.zh: 乃自以為建王四世孫，改國號曰唐。

translations.literal: He then took himself to be the fourth-generation descendant of Prince Jian and changed the state title to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he styled himself the fourth-generation descendant of Prince Jian and changed the dynastic name to Tang.

sentences.zh: 立唐高祖、太宗廟，追尊四代祖恪為孝靜皇帝，廟號定宗；

translations.literal: He established temples to Tang Gaozu and Taizong, and posthumously honored his fourth-generation ancestor Ke as Emperor Xiaojing, temple name Dingzong;
translations.idiomatic: He founded temples to Tang Gaozu and Taizong and posthumously honored his fourth-generation ancestor Ke as Emperor Xiaojing, with the temple name Dingzong;

sentences.zh: 曾祖超為孝平皇帝，廟號成宗；

translations.literal: his great-grandfather Chao as Emperor Xiaoping, temple name Chengzong;
translations.idiomatic: his great-grandfather Chao as Emperor Xiaoping, temple name Chengzong;

sentences.zh: 祖誌孝安皇帝，廟號惠宗；

translations.literal: his grandfather Zhi as Emperor Xiao'an, temple name Huizong;
translations.idiomatic: his grandfather Zhi as Emperor Xiao'an, temple name Huizong;

sentences.zh: 考榮孝德皇帝，廟號慶宗。

translations.literal: and his father Rong as Emperor Xiaode, temple name Qingzong.
translations.idiomatic: and his father Rong as Emperor Xiaode, temple name Qingzong.

sentences.zh: 奉徐溫為義父，徐氏子孫皆封王、公，女封郡、縣主。

translations.literal: He honored Xu Wen as his adoptive father; Xu's sons and grandsons were all enfeoffed as kings and dukes, and daughters as commandery and county princesses.
translations.idiomatic: He acknowledged Xu Wen as his adoptive father, enfeoffed all of Xu's male descendants as princes or dukes, and titled his daughters as commandery or county princesses.

sentences.zh: 以門下侍郎張居詠、中書侍郎李建勛、右僕射張延翰同平章事。

translations.literal: He made Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Juyong, Vice Director of the Chancellery Li Jianxun, and Right Vice Director Zhang Yanhan co-directors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhang Juyong, Li Jianxun, and Zhang Yanhan joint directors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以步騎八萬講武於銅橋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, with eighty thousand infantry and cavalry he conducted military exercises at Tong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he reviewed eighty thousand foot and horse troops at Tong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 楊溥卒於丹陽宮。

translations.literal: Yang Pu died at the Danyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu died in the Danyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 溥子璉為吳太子時，以女妻之，及篡國，封其女永興公主。

translations.literal: When Pu's son Lian was crown prince of Wu, he gave his daughter in marriage to Bian. When Bian usurped the state he enfeoffed the daughter as Princess of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: While Pu's son Lian was still crown prince of Wu, Lian had given his daughter to Bian in marriage. After the founding of the new dynasty, Bian created her Princess of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 女聞人呼公主，則嗚咽流涕而辭，宮中皆憐之。

translations.literal: When the daughter heard people address her as princess, she would sob and weep and decline the title; all in the palace pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she heard herself called princess she wept and refused the title, and everyone in the palace pitied her.

sentences.zh: 溥卒，以璉為康化軍節度使，已而以疾卒。

translations.literal: When Pu died, he made Lian military governor of the Kanghua Army; before long Lian also died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Pu's death he appointed Lian military governor of the Kanghua army, but Lian soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，郊祀昊天上帝於圓丘，禮畢，群臣請上尊號。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he sacrificed to the August Lord of Heaven at the Round Mound. When the rites were finished the ministers requested that a honorific title be bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he offered the suburban sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound. When the ceremony ended, his ministers asked that he take an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 曰：「尊號非古也。

translations.literal: He said: "Honorific titles are not ancient."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Honorific titles are not an ancient practice."

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: " He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused.

sentences.zh: 州、縣言民孝悌五代同居者七家，皆表門閭，復其徭役；

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties reported seven households of the people whose filial piety and brotherliness extended through five generations living together; all were marked at their gate and lane, and their corvée labor was remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties reported seven families in which five generations had lived together in filial harmony. Each household was honored at its gate and exempted from labor service;

sentences.zh: 其尤盛者江州陳氏，宗族七百口，每食設廣席，長幼以次坐而共食，有畜犬百餘，共一牢食，一犬不至，諸犬為之不食。

translations.literal: the most outstanding being the Chen clan of Jiang Prefecture: seven hundred mouths in the clan. At each meal they spread a broad mat; elders and juniors sat in order and ate together. They kept more than a hundred dogs that ate from one trough; if one dog did not come, the other dogs would not eat for its sake.
translations.idiomatic: the most remarkable being the Chen clan of Jiangzhou, seven hundred strong. At every meal they set a long table and ate in order of age. They kept more than a hundred dogs fed from a single trough; if one dog failed to appear, the rest would not eat until it came.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，晉安州節度使李金全叛，送款於，遣鄂州屯營使李承裕迎之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year Jin's military governor of An Prefecture, Li Jinquan, rebelled and sent allegiance to him. He dispatched E Prefecture encampment commissioner Li Chengyu to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year Li Jinquan, Jin's military governor of Anzhou, rebelled and submitted to Tang. Bian sent Li Chengyu of the Ezhou garrison to receive him.

sentences.zh: 承裕與晉將馬全節、安審暉戰安陸南，三戰皆敗，承裕與裨將段處恭皆死，都監杜光鄴及其兵五百人被執，送於京師，高祖厚賜之，遣還。

translations.literal: Chengyu fought south of Anlu with the Jin generals Ma Quanjie and An Shenhui; in three battles he was defeated. Chengyu and the lieutenant Duan Chugong both died. The overseer Du Guangye and his five hundred troops were captured and sent to the capital. Gaozu richly rewarded them and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyu fought Ma Quanjie and An Shenhui of Jin south of Anlu and lost three engagements in a row. Chengyu and his lieutenant Duan Chugong were killed. The commander Du Guangye and five hundred men were taken prisoner and sent to the Jin capital, where Emperor Gaozu treated them generously and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 致書高祖，復送光鄴等，請以敗軍行法，高祖又遣之，以甲士臨淮拒之，乃止。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Gaozu and again returned Guangye and the others, requesting that the defeated army be dealt with by law. Gaozu again sent them back. With armored troops at the Huai he barred them, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Bian wrote to Jin's Emperor Gaozu, returned Guangye and his men again, and asked that the defeated troops be punished under military law. Gaozu sent them back once more. Bian posted armored troops on the Huai to block them, and the exchange finally ended.

sentences.zh: 六年，吳越國火，焚其宮室、府庫，甲兵皆盡，群臣請乘其弊攻之，不許，遣使吊問，厚赒其乏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year a fire in the state of Wuyue burned its palaces and treasuries; armor and weapons were all consumed. The ministers requested to strike while it was weakened; he did not permit it but sent envoys to offer condolences and richly relieved their want.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year fire destroyed the palaces and treasuries of Wuyue and consumed its arms. His ministers urged an attack while the enemy was weak, but he refused, sent envoys of condolence, and gave generous relief.

sentences.zh: 錢氏自吳時素為敵國，見天下亂久，常厭用兵，及將篡國，先與錢氏約和，歸其所執將士，錢氏亦歸吳敗將，遂通好不絕。

translations.literal: The Qian clan had since Wu times been a constant enemy state. Seeing the realm long in disorder, they often wearied of using troops. When Bian was about to usurp the state he first made peace with the Qian clan, returning the officers and soldiers they held; the Qian clan also returned Wu's defeated generals, and thus friendly intercourse never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian house of Wuyue had been Wu's rival since old times. With the empire long in chaos, both sides had grown weary of war. Before seizing the throne Bian made peace with Wuyue, returning captured officers and men; Wuyue returned Wu's defeated generals in turn, and friendly relations continued thereafter.

sentences.zh: 昪客馮延巳好論兵大言，嘗誚曰：「田舍翁安能成大事！

translations.literal: Bian's retainer Feng Yansi loved to discuss warfare in grand words and once mocked him, saying: "How can a rustic old fellow accomplish great deeds!"
translations.idiomatic: Bian's adviser Feng Yansi loved bold talk of war and once sneered, "What great deed can a country bumpkin accomplish!"

sentences.zh: 」而志在守吳舊地而已，無復經營之略也，然吳人亦賴以休息。

translations.literal: " Yet his aim was only to hold Wu's old territory; he had no further plans for expansion, yet the people of Wu also relied on this to rest.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Bian aimed only to hold Wu's former lands and had no further ambition of conquest, and the people of Wu were able to recover their breath because of it.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年五十六，謚曰光文肅武孝高皇帝，廟號烈祖，陵曰永陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, age fifty-six. His posthumous title was Emperor Guangwen Suwu Xiaogao; his temple name Liezu; his tomb Yongling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died at fifty-six. He was posthumously titled Emperor Guangwen Suwu Xiaogao, temple name Liezu, and buried at Yongling.

sentences.zh: 子景立。

translations.literal: His son Jing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 景，初名景通，長子也。

translations.literal: Jing, originally named Jingtong, was the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, originally named Jingtong, was his eldest son.

sentences.zh: 既立，又改名璟。

translations.literal: After he was established he again changed his name to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession he changed his name to Jing.

sentences.zh: 徐溫死，專政，以為兵部尚書、參知政事。

translations.literal: When Xu Wen died, Bian monopolized government and made him Minister of War and Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Wen's death, when Bian held sole power, he appointed Jing Minister of War and participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 明年，鎮金陵，留景為司徒、同平章事，與宋齊丘、王令謀居廣陵，輔楊溥。

translations.literal: The next year he stationed himself at Jinling, leaving Jing as Grand Mentor and Co-Director, with Song Qiqiu and Wang Lingmou residing at Guangling to assist Yang Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Bian took up post at Jinling and left Jing in Guangling as Grand Mentor and co-director, with Song Qiqiu and Wang Lingmou to assist Yang Pu.

sentences.zh: 將篡國，召景歸金陵為副都統。

translations.literal: When he was about to usurp the state he summoned Jing back to Jinling as deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian prepared to seize the throne he recalled Jing to Jinling as deputy overall commander.

sentences.zh: 立，封齊王。

translations.literal: When Bian was established he enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Upon founding his dynasty, Bian created him Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 卒，嗣位，改元保大。

translations.literal: When Bian died, Jing succeeded to the throne and changed the era name to Baoda.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian died, Jing succeeded and proclaimed the era name Baoda.

sentences.zh: 尊母宋氏為皇太后，妃鐘氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He honored his mother the Song clan as Empress Dowager and his consort the Zhong clan as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his mother, Lady Song, as empress dowager and his consort, Lady Zhong, as empress.

sentences.zh: 封弟壽王景遂為燕王，宣城王景達鄂王，景逷前未王，為保寧王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his younger brother the Prince of Shou Jing Sui as Prince of Yan, the Prince of Xuancheng Jing Da as Prince of E, and Jing You, who had not previously held a princedom, as Prince of Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: He created his brother Jing Sui, Prince of Shou, Prince of Yan; Jing Da, Prince of Xuancheng, Prince of E; and Jing You, who had not yet held a title, Prince of Baoning.

sentences.zh: 秋，改封景遂齊王、諸道兵馬元帥、太尉、中書令，景達為燕王、副元帥，盟於柩前，約兄弟世世繼立。

translations.literal: In autumn he changed Jing Sui's enfeoffment to Prince of Qi, Grand Marshal of All Circuits' Troops and Horses, Grand Mentor, and Director of the Chancellery; Jing Da became Prince of Yan and Deputy Grand Marshal. They swore an oath before the coffin that brothers would succeed one another generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he recreated Jing Sui as Prince of Qi, grand marshal of all circuits, Grand Mentor, and director of the Chancellery, and made Jing Da Prince of Yan and deputy grand marshal. Before their father's coffin they swore that the brothers would take the throne in turn, generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 封其子冀南昌王、江都尹。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his son Ji as Prince of Nanchang and prefect of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He created his son Ji Prince of Nanchang and prefect of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，破虔州妖賊張遇賢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he defeated the demonic rebel of Qian Prefecture, Zhang Yuxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he crushed Zhang Yuxian, the sorcerer-rebel of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇賢，循州羅縣小吏也。

translations.literal: Yuxian was a petty clerk of Luoxian in Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian had been a minor clerk in Luoxian, Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，有神降羅縣民家，與人言禍福輒中。

translations.literal: At first a spirit descended into a commoner's house in Luoxian; when it spoke to people of fortune and misfortune it was invariably correct.
translations.idiomatic: At first a spirit possessed a household in Luoxian and foretold fortune and misfortune with uncanny accuracy.

sentences.zh: 遇賢禱之，神曰：「遇賢是羅漢，可留事我。

translations.literal: Yuxian prayed to it. The spirit said: "Yuxian is a luohan; he may remain to serve me."
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian prayed to the spirit, which said, "Yuxian is a luohan—let him stay and serve me."

sentences.zh: 」是時，南海劉龑死，子玢初立，嶺南盜賊起，群盜千餘人未有所統，問神當為主者，神言遇賢，遂共推為帥。

translations.literal: " At that time Liu Yan of the Southern Sea died and his son Bin had just been enthroned. Bandits rose in Lingnan; more than a thousand robbers had as yet no leader. They asked the spirit who should be master, and the spirit named Yuxian; they thereupon jointly made him commander.
translations.idiomatic: " About then Liu Yan of the Southern Han died and his son Bin had just taken the throne. Bandits rose throughout Lingnan. More than a thousand outlaws lacked a leader, asked the spirit who should rule them, and were told Yuxian. They made him their chief.

sentences.zh: 遇賢自號中天八國王，改元永樂，置官屬，群賊盜皆絳衣，攻剽嶺外，問神所向，神曰：「當過嶺取虔州。

translations.literal: Yuxian styled himself King of the Eight Kingdoms of the Central Heaven, changed the era name to Yongle, established officials, and all the bandit robbers wore crimson clothes. They raided beyond the ranges. Asking the spirit where to go, the spirit said: "You should cross the ranges and take Qian Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian styled himself King of the Eight Kingdoms of the Central Heaven, proclaimed the era Yongle, appointed officials, and dressed his followers in crimson. They plundered the far south. When they asked the spirit where to march, it answered, "Cross the mountains and take Qianzhou."

sentences.zh: 」遂襲南康，節度賈浩不能禦。

translations.literal: " They then raided Nankang; the military governor Jia Hao could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: " They struck Nankang, and the military governor Jia Hao could not hold them off.

sentences.zh: 遇賢據白雲洞，造宮室，有眾十餘萬，連陷諸縣。

translations.literal: Yuxian occupied White Cloud Cave, built palaces, had a host of more than a hundred thousand, and in succession captured the counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian seized White Cloud Cave, built palaces there, gathered more than a hundred thousand followers, and overran county after county.

sentences.zh: 景遣洪州營屯虞候嚴思、通事舍人邊鎬率兵攻之。

translations.literal: Jing dispatched Hong Prefecture encampment awaiting-commander Yan Si and Imperial Diarist Bian Hao to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Yan Si of the Hongzhou garrison and the diarist Bian Hao at the head of an army against him.

sentences.zh: 遇賢問神，神不復語，群盜皆懼，遂執遇賢以降。

translations.literal: Yuxian questioned the spirit; the spirit spoke no more. All the bandits were afraid and thereupon seized Yuxian and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxian consulted the spirit, but it would not answer. Terrified, his followers seized him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，宋齊丘為謀篡楊氏最有力，及事成，乃陽入九華山，屢招之，乃出。

translations.literal: At first Song Qiqiu had been most forceful in plotting to usurp the Yang clan. When the deed was done he pretended to enter Jiuhua Mountain; repeatedly summoned, he then came out.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu had been the strongest advocate of overthrowing the Yang house. Once the deed was done he pretended to retire to Jiuhua Mountain, but repeated summons brought him back to court.

sentences.zh: 僭號，未幾，齊丘以病罷相，出為洪州節度使。

translations.literal: When Bian assumed the imperial title, before long Qiqiu was dismissed from the chancellorship on grounds of illness and went out as military governor of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after Bian took the imperial title, Qiqiu resigned the chancellorship on grounds of illness and became military governor of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景立，復召為相，而陳覺、魏岑等皆為齊丘所引用。

translations.literal: When Jing was established he again summoned him as chief minister, while Chen Jue, Wei Cen, and others had all been introduced by Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing came to the throne he recalled Qiqiu as chief minister. Chen Jue, Wei Cen, and others had all risen through Qiqiu's patronage.

sentences.zh: 而岑與覺有隙，譖覺於景，左遷少府監。

translations.literal: But Cen and Jue had a rift; Cen slandered Jue to Jing, and Jue was demoted to director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Cen and Jue fell out, and Cen slandered Jue to the emperor, who demoted Jue to director of the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 齊丘亦罷相為浙西節度使。

translations.literal: Qiqiu also left the chancellorship and became military governor of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu was dismissed as well and sent out as military governor of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 齊丘不得意，願復歸九華山，賜號九華先生，封青陽公，食青陽一縣。

translations.literal: Qiqiu was discontent, wished to return again to Jiuhua Mountain, was granted the style Master of Jiuhua, enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyang, and received the revenue of one Qingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Disappointed, Qiqiu asked to return to Jiuhua Mountain. Jing granted him the title Master of Jiuhua, created him Duke of Qingyang, and assigned him the revenues of one county.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，閩人連重遇、朱文進弒其君王延羲，文進自立。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year the men of Min, Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin, assassinated their ruler Wang Yanxi; Wenjin established himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin of Min murdered their ruler Wang Yanxi, and Wenjin seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 是時，延羲弟延政亦自立於建州，國號殷。

translations.literal: At this time Yanxi's younger brother Yanzheng also established himself at Jian Prefecture, with the state title Yin.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Yanxi's brother Yanzheng declared himself ruler at Jianzhou under the state name Yin.

sentences.zh: 王氏兄弟連兵累年，閩大亂，景因其亂遣查文徽及待詔臧循發兵攻建州。

translations.literal: The Wang brothers fought in succession for years; Min was in great disorder. Jing, taking advantage of the disorder, dispatched Zha Wenhui and the awaiting-edict Zang Xun to raise troops and attack Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang brothers had fought for years and Min was in chaos. Jing seized the chance to send Zha Wenhui and the awaiting-edict Zang Xun against Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 延政聞唐且攻之，遣人紿福州曰：「唐兵助我討賊矣。

translations.literal: Yanzheng heard that Tang was about to attack him and sent men to deceive Fuzhou, saying: "Tang troops are helping me punish the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Tang was marching against him, Yanzheng sent agents to deceive Fuzhou with the message, "Tang troops are coming to help me punish the rebels."

sentences.zh: 」福州信之，共殺文進等以降，延政遣其從子繼昌守福州。

translations.literal: " Fuzhou believed this, jointly killed Wenjin and the others in order to surrender, and Yanzheng dispatched his nephew Jichang to hold Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou took the bait, banded together to kill Wenjin and his followers and submit, and Yanzheng posted his nephew Jichang to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 文徽軍屯建陽，福州將李仁達殺王繼昌自稱留後，泉州將留從效亦殺其刺史黃紹頗，皆送款於文徽。

translations.literal: Wen Hui's army was encamped at Jianyang. The Fuzhou general Li Renda killed Wang Jichang and declared himself military commissioner. The Quanzhou general Liu Congxiao also killed his prefect Huang Shaobian. All sent pledges of submission to Wen Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui's army was stationed at Jianyang when the Fuzhou commander Li Renda killed Wang Jichang and proclaimed himself military governor. The Quanzhou commander Liu Congxiao likewise killed his prefect Huang Shaobian. Both men then offered their allegiance to Wen Hui.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，文徽乘勝克建、汀、泉、漳四州，景分延平、劍浦、富沙三縣，置劍州，遷王延政之族於金陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year Wen Hui, riding victory, captured the four prefectures of Jian, Ting, Quan, and Zhang. Jing divided the three counties of Yanping, Jianpu, and Fusha to establish Jian Prefecture and moved the clan of Wang Yanzheng to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year Wen Hui pressed his advantage and took Jian, Ting, Quan, and Zhang. Jing carved Yanping, Jianpu, and Fusha out as a new Jian Prefecture and resettled Wang Yanzheng's entire clan at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 以延政為饒州節度使、李仁達為福州節度使、留從效為清源軍節度使。

translations.literal: He made Yanzheng military governor of Raozhou, Li Renda military governor of Fuzhou, and Liu Congxiao military governor of the Qingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzheng was appointed military governor of Raozhou, Li Renda of Fuzhou, and Liu Congxiao of the Qingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 景遂欲罷兵，而查文徽、陳覺等皆言：「仁達等余孽猶在，不若乘勝盡取之。

translations.literal: Jing then wished to halt the army, but Zha Wen Hui, Chen Jue, and the others all said: "The remnant followers of Li Renda and the rest are still there; better to ride the victory and take them all."
translations.idiomatic: Jing then wanted to end the campaign, but Zha Wen Hui, Chen Jue, and others argued, "Li Renda and his followers are still at large—we should press our advantage and finish them off."

sentences.zh: 」陳覺自言可不用尺兵致仁達等。

translations.literal: " Chen Jue himself said he could bring Li Renda and the rest without using a foot of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue went further, claiming he could win over Li Renda and the others without raising a single soldier.

sentences.zh: 景以覺為宣諭使，召仁達朝金陵，仁達不從。

translations.literal: Jing made Jue an envoy of instruction and summoned Renda to court at Jinling; Renda did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Jing appointed Jue as imperial envoy and summoned Renda to Jinling, but Renda refused to come.

sentences.zh: 覺慚，還至建州，矯命發汀、建、信、撫州兵攻仁達。

translations.literal: Ashamed, Jue returned to Jian Prefecture and on forged orders mobilized troops from Ting, Jian, Xin, and Fu prefectures to attack Renda.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Jue went back to Jian Prefecture and, on forged orders, raised armies from Ting, Jian, Xin, and Fu to attack Renda.

sentences.zh: 時魏岑安撫漳、泉，聞覺起兵，亦擅發兵會覺。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Cen was pacifying Zhang and Quan; hearing that Jue had raised troops, he also on his own authority mobilized troops to join Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cen was then pacifying Zhang and Quan. When he heard that Jue had taken the field, he too mobilized troops on his own authority and marched to join him.

sentences.zh: 景大怒，馮延巳等為言：「兵業行，不可止。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly angered. Feng Yansi and others spoke on their behalf, saying: "The troops have already set out and cannot be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Jing was furious, but Feng Yansi and others pleaded their case: "The armies are already in motion and cannot be recalled."

sentences.zh: 」乃以王崇文為招討使、王建封為副使，益兵以會之，以延魯、魏岑、陳覺皆為監軍使。

translations.literal: " Then he appointed Wang Chongwen as campaign commander and Wang Jianfeng as deputy, added troops to join them, and made Yan Lu, Wei Cen, and Chen Jue all army supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then appointed Wang Chongwen as campaign commander with Wang Jianfeng as his deputy, reinforced the expedition, and made Yan Lu, Wei Cen, and Chen Jue army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 仁達送款於吳越，吳越以兵三萬應仁達。

translations.literal: Renda sent pledges of submission to Wuyue, and Wuyue sent thirty thousand troops to support Renda.
translations.idiomatic: Renda appealed to Wuyue for aid, and Wuyue answered with thirty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 覺等爭功，進退不相應，延魯與吳越兵先戰，大敗而走，諸軍皆潰歸。

translations.literal: Jue and the others competed for merit; advance and retreat did not coordinate. Yan Lu fought first with the Wuyue troops, was greatly defeated and fled, and all the armies collapsed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jue and his colleagues squabbled over credit and failed to coordinate their movements. Yan Lu clashed first with the Wuyue army, suffered a crushing defeat, and fled; the rest of the force broke and retreated.

sentences.zh: 景怒，遣使者鎖覺、延魯至金陵。

translations.literal: Jing was angry and dispatched envoys to chain Jue and Yan Lu and bring them to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jing sent envoys to put Jue and Yan Lu in chains and haul them back to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 而馮延巳方為宰相，宋齊丘復自九華召為太傅，為稍解之，乃流覺蘄州、延魯舒州。

translations.literal: But Feng Yansi was then chancellor, and Song Qiqiu had again been recalled from Jiuhua as Grand Preceptor; on their behalf they somewhat mitigated matters, and Jue was exiled to Qizhou and Yan Lu to Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yansi was still chancellor, however, and Song Qiqiu had just been recalled from Mount Jiuhua as Grand Preceptor; they interceded and won a measure of leniency, so Jue was banished to Qizhou and Yan Lu to Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓熙載上書切諫，請誅覺等，齊丘惡之，貶熙載和州司馬。

translations.literal: Han Xizai submitted a memorial with sharp remonstrance, requesting the execution of Jue and the others. Qiqiu resented this and demoted Xizai to staff officer of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai memorialized the throne in blunt protest, demanding that Jue and his associates be put to death. Qiqiu took offense and had Xizai demoted to staff officer at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹陷京師，中國無主，而景方以覺等疲兵東南，不暇北顧。

translations.literal: That year the Khitans captured the capital; China had no ruler, yet Jing was just then wearing out his troops in the southeast because of Jue and the others, with no leisure to look to the north.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Khitans took the capital and the Central Plains were left without a sovereign, but Jing was still draining his armies in the southeast over Jue's fiasco and had no strength to spare for the north.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞江文蔚劾奏宰相馮延巳、諫議大夫魏岑亂政，與覺等同罪而不見貶黜，言甚切直。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Jiang Wenwei memorialized to impeach Chancellor Feng Yansi and Remonstrance Official Wei Cen for misgovernment, saying they shared the same guilt as Jue and the others yet had not been demoted; his words were very blunt.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief Jiang Wenwei impeached Chancellor Feng Yansi and Remonstrance Official Wei Cen for corrupt governance, arguing that they were as guilty as Jue and his circle yet had escaped punishment. His language was scathing.

sentences.zh: 景大怒，自答其疏，貶文蔚江州司士參軍，亦罷延巳為少傅、岑為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly angered, personally answered his memorial, demoted Wenwei to staff officer of Jiangzhou, and also removed Yansi as Junior Tutor and Cen as crown prince's launderer.
translations.idiomatic: Jing flew into a rage and answered the memorial himself, demoting Wenwei to a minor post in Jiangzhou and stripping Yansi of his chancellorship to make him Junior Tutor and Cen crown prince's attendant.

sentences.zh: 五年，以景遂為太弟；

translations.literal: In the fifth year he made Jingsui Grand Younger Brother;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jing named Jingsui Grand Younger Brother;

sentences.zh: 景達為元帥，封齊王；

translations.literal: Jingda as commander-in-chief, enfeoffed as Prince of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: made Jingda commander-in-chief and enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi;

sentences.zh: 南昌王冀為副元帥，封燕王。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanchang Ji as deputy commander-in-chief, enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Prince of Nanchang Ji deputy commander-in-chief, enfeoffing him as Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣使來聘，以兵部尚書賈潭報聘。

translations.literal: The Khitans sent envoys on a friendly mission, and he sent Minister of War Jia Tan on a return mission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans sent envoys on a courtesy visit, Jing replied by dispatching Minister of War Jia Tan on a return mission.

sentences.zh: 六年，漢李守貞反河中，遣其客將朱元來求援，景以潤州節度使李金全為北面行營招撫使，兵攻沭陽，聞守貞已敗，乃還。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Li Shouzhen of Han rebelled at Hezhong and sent his client general Zhu Yuan to seek aid. Jing made Runzhou military governor Li Jinquan commander of the Northern Expeditionary Pacification Office and sent troops to attack Shuyang; hearing that Shouzhen had already been defeated, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Li Shouzhen of Later Han rebelled at Hezhong and sent his client general Zhu Yuan to ask for help. Jing appointed Runzhou governor Li Jinquan to lead a northern expedition and attack Shuyang, but when word came that Shouzhen had already been crushed, the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢隱帝少，中國衰弱，淮北群盜多送款於景，景遣皇甫暉出海、泗諸州招納之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yin of Han was young and China was weak; many bandits north of the Huai sent pledges of submission to Jing, and Jing dispatched Huangfu Hui to go out to the Hai and Si prefectures to recruit and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han emperor Yin was still a boy and the Central Plains were in decline. Many bandit bands north of the Huai offered their allegiance to Jing, and he sent Huangfu Hui into the Hai and Si region to recruit them.

sentences.zh: 八年，福州詐言「吳越戍兵亂，殺李仁達而遁」，遣人請建州節度使查文徽，文徽與劍州刺史陳誨下舟閩江趨應之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Fuzhou falsely reported, "The Wuyue garrison troops mutinied, killed Li Renda, and fled," and sent men to invite Jianzhou military governor Zha Wen Hui. Wen Hui and Jianzhou prefect Chen Hui disembarked on the Min River to hurry and respond.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Fuzhou sent a false report that Wuyue's garrison had mutinied, killed Li Renda, and fled, then invited Jianzhou governor Zha Wen Hui to take the city. Wen Hui and Jianzhou prefect Chen Hui sailed down the Min River at once to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 福州以兵出迎。

translations.literal: Fuzhou sent troops out to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou marched troops out to greet them.

sentences.zh: 誨曰：「閩人多詐難信，宜駐江岸徐圖之。

translations.literal: Hui said: "The people of Min are much given to deceit and hard to trust; it is best to halt on the riverbank and plan slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui warned, "The Min people are treacherous and cannot be trusted—we should hold the riverbank and proceed with caution."

sentences.zh: 」文徽曰：「久則生變，乘其未定，亟取之。

translations.literal: " Wen Hui said: "If too long, change will arise; while they are still unsettled, take it quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui replied that delay would invite trouble and that they should strike while the city was still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 」留誨屯江口，進至西門，伏兵發，文徽被擒。

translations.literal: " He left Hui encamped at the river mouth, advanced to the West Gate; ambush troops rose and Wen Hui was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He left Chen Hui at the river mouth and pressed on to the West Gate, where hidden troops sprang up and seized Wen Hui.

sentences.zh: 誨與越人戰，大敗之，獲其將馬先進。

translations.literal: Hui fought with the Yue men and greatly defeated them, capturing their general Ma Xianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui fought the Wuyue troops and routed them, taking their general Ma Xianjin prisoner.

sentences.zh: 景送先進還越，越亦歸景文徽。

translations.literal: Jing sent Xianjin back to Yue, and Yue also returned Wen Hui to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Xianjin back to Wuyue, and Wuyue in turn released Wen Hui to him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，楚王馬希廣為其弟希萼所弒，希萼自立。

translations.literal: That year Prince of Chu Ma Xiguang was assassinated by his younger brother Xi'e, who established himself.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Chu ruler Ma Xiguang was murdered by his younger brother Xi'e, who then seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，楚人囚希萼於衡山，立其弟希崇，附於景，楚國大亂。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year the Chu people imprisoned Xi'e on Heng Mountain, enthroned his younger brother Xichong, submitted to Jing, and the state of Chu fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year the Chu people imprisoned Xi'e on Mount Heng, raised his brother Xichong to the throne, and submitted to Jing as Chu descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 景遣信州刺史邊鎬攻楚，破潭州，盡遷馬氏之族於金陵。

translations.literal: Jing dispatched Xingzhou prefect Bian Hao to attack Chu, captured Tanzhou, and moved the entire Ma clan to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Xingzhou governor Bian Hao against Chu. Bian took Tanzhou and resettled the entire Ma clan at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 景以希萼為洪州節度使，希崇舒州節度使，以邊鎬為湖南節度使。

translations.literal: Jing made Xi'e military governor of Hongzhou, Xichong military governor of Shuzhou, and Bian Hao military governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing appointed Xi'e military governor of Hongzhou, Xichong of Shuzhou, and Bian Hao of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十年，分洪州高安、清江、萬載、上高四縣，置筠州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he separated the four counties of Gao'an, Qingjiang, WanZai, and Shanggao from Hongzhou and established Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he carved Gao'an, Qingjiang, WanZai, and Shanggao out of Hongzhou to create Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以馮延巳、孫忌為左、右僕射同平章事。

translations.literal: He made Feng Yansi and Sun Ji Left and Right Grand Counselors with concurrent chief minister status.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Feng Yansi and Sun Ji Left and Right Grand Counselors with the rank of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 廣州劉晟乘楚之亂，取桂管，景遣將軍張巒出兵爭之，不克。

translations.literal: Liu Sheng of Guangzhou took advantage of Chu's disorder to seize the Gui administrative region. Jing dispatched General Zhang Luan to lead troops to contest it but did not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng of Guangzhou exploited the turmoil in Chu to seize the Gui region. Jing sent General Zhang Luan to contest the ground but failed to recover it.

sentences.zh: 楚地新定，其府庫空虛，宰相馮延巳以克楚為功，不欲取費於國，乃重斂其民以給軍，楚人皆怨而叛，其將劉言攻邊鎬，鎬不能守，遁歸。

translations.literal: The Chu region had just been pacified and its treasuries were empty. Chancellor Feng Yansi, taking the conquest of Chu as his achievement, did not wish to draw expenses from the state and instead heavily levied the people to supply the army; all Chu people resented and rebelled. Their general Liu Yan attacked Bian Hao; Hao could not hold and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had only just been pacified and its coffers were bare. Chancellor Feng Yansi, eager to claim credit for the conquest, refused to spend imperial funds and instead squeezed the local population to feed the army. Resentment spread until the Chu general Liu Yan rose against Bian Hao, who could not hold the province and fled home.

sentences.zh: 十一年，金陵大火逾月。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year a great fire in Jinling lasted more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a great fire raged in Jinling for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 十二年，大饑，民多疫死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year there was great famine, and many people died of plague.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year famine struck, and plague carried off great numbers of people.

sentences.zh: 十三年十一月，周師南征，詔曰：「蠢爾淮甸，敢拒大邦，盜據一方，僭稱偽號。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year Zhou troops marched south on campaign. The edict said: "You foolish ones of the Huai region dare to resist the great state, unlawfully hold one region, and usurp a false title."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year the Zhou army marched south. The imperial edict declared, "You wretches of the Huai region dare defy a great power, seize territory by force, and presume upon a usurper's title."

sentences.zh: 晉、漢之代，寰海未寧，而乃招納叛亡，朋助兇逆。

translations.literal: In the transitions of Jin and Han all within the seas was not settled, yet you recruit and harbor fugitive rebels and ally yourselves with vicious wrongdoers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin and Han dynasties fell and the realm was still unsettled, you sheltered fugitive rebels and abetted violent traitors.

sentences.zh: 金全之據安陸，守貞之叛河中，大起師徒，來為應援。

translations.literal: Jin Quan held Anlu, Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong—you greatly raised armies and came in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Quan seized Anlu and Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, you raised great armies to aid them.

sentences.zh: 迫奪閩、越，塗炭湘、潭，至於應接慕容，憑陵徐部，沭陽之役，曲直可知。

translations.literal: You forced seizure of Min and Yue, ravaged Xiang and Tan, even received Murong, encroached on the Xu region—the battle of Shuyang shows clearly who was in the right.
translations.idiomatic: You wrested Min and Yue by force, laid waste to Xiang and Tan, harbored Murong Yanchao, and encroached on the Xu region—the battle at Shuyang alone shows where justice lay.

sentences.zh: 勾誘契丹，入為邊患，結連並壘，實我世仇。

translations.literal: You enticed the Khitans to enter as border menace, linked with Bing and frontier strongholds—truly our hereditary enemies.
translations.idiomatic: You colluded with the Khitans to threaten the frontier, forged ties with Bingzhou and the northern fortresses—enemies of ours across generations.

sentences.zh: 罪惡難名，人神共憤。

translations.literal: Your crimes are beyond naming; gods and men alike are furious.
translations.idiomatic: Your crimes beggar description, and both heaven and earth cry out against you.

sentences.zh: 」乃拜李穀為行營都部署，攻自壽州始。

translations.literal: " Then he appointed Li Gu as overall commander of the expeditionary camp; the attack began from Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With that the court appointed Li Gu supreme commander of the expedition, and the assault opened from Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋齊丘為洪州節度使，景召齊丘還金陵，以劉彥貞為神武統軍，劉仁贍為清淮軍節度使，以距周師。

translations.literal: At that time Song Qiqiu was military governor of Hongzhou. Jing recalled Qiqiu to Jinling, made Liu Yanzhen commander of the Divine Martial Army and Liu Renshan military governor of the Qinghuai Army to resist the Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu was then military governor of Hongzhou. Jing recalled him to Jinling and put Liu Yanzhen in command of the Divine Martial Army and Liu Renshan in charge of the Qinghuai Army to meet the Zhou invasion.

sentences.zh: 李穀曰：「吾無水戰之具，而使淮兵斷正陽浮橋，則我背腹受敵。

translations.literal: Li Gu said: "I have no equipment for water warfare, and if I have Huai troops cut off the Zhengyang floating bridge, then I will receive enemies on back and belly."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu said, "We lack the means to fight on the water. If Southern Tang forces sever the floating bridge at Zhengyang, we will be trapped between enemies front and rear."

sentences.zh: 」乃焚其芻糧，退屯正陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he burned their fodder and grain and withdrew to encamp at Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: So he burned his fodder and supplies and pulled back to make camp at Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 是時世宗親征，行至圉鎮，聞谷退軍，曰：「吾軍卻，唐兵必追之。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong personally marched on campaign; reaching Yuzhen, he heard that Gu had withdrawn the army and said: "When our army retreats, Tang troops will surely pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was leading the campaign in person. When he reached Yuzhen and learned that Li Gu had pulled his forces back, he said, "The moment our army withdraws, the Southern Tang will come after us."

sentences.zh: 」遣李重進急趨正陽，曰：「唐兵且至，宜急擊之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Li Chongjin to hurry toward Zhengyang, saying: "Tang troops are about to arrive; they should be struck quickly."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Chongjin racing toward Zhengyang with orders to attack at once, saying the Southern Tang would be arriving soon.

sentences.zh: 」劉彥貞等聞谷退軍，果以為怯，急追之。

translations.literal: Liu Yanzhen and the others, hearing that Gu had withdrawn the army, indeed took it as cowardice and pursued in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzhen and his commanders, hearing of Li Gu's retreat, assumed the Zhou were fleeing and gave chase.

sentences.zh: 比及正陽，而重進先至，軍未及食而戰，彥貞等遂敗。

translations.literal: When they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin had already arrived first; the army had not yet eaten when they gave battle, and Yanzhen and the others were thus defeated.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Zhengyang, Li Chongjin was already there. The Zhou soldiers fought before they had even taken a meal, and Liu Yanzhen's force was routed.

sentences.zh: 彥貞之兵施利刃於拒馬，維以鐵索；

translations.literal: Yanzhen's troops placed sharp blades on cheval-de-frise and bound them with iron chains;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzhen's men mounted sharp blades on barricades and lashed them together with iron chains;

sentences.zh: 又刻木為獸，號「捷馬牌」；

translations.literal: They also carved wood into beasts, calling them "Victory Horse Placards";
translations.idiomatic: They also carved wooden beasts and called them "Swift Horse Banners";

sentences.zh: 以皮囊布鐵蒺藜於地。

translations.literal: They used leather sacks to spread iron caltrops on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: They scattered iron caltrops across the field in leather pouches.

sentences.zh: 周兵見而知其怯，一鼓敗之。

translations.literal: Zhou troops saw and knew their cowardice; with one drumroll they defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou soldiers recognized at a glance how timid these preparations were and routed them with a single charge.

sentences.zh: 世宗營於淝水之陽，徙浮橋於下蔡。

translations.literal: Shizong encamped on the south bank of the Fei River and moved the floating bridge to Xia Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong made camp south of the Fei River and relocated the floating bridge downstream to Xia Cai.

sentences.zh: 景遣林仁肇等爭之不得，而周師取滁州。

translations.literal: Jing dispatched Lin Renzhao and others to contest it but could not succeed, and Zhou troops took Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing sent Lin Renzhao and others to seize the bridge but failed, and the Zhou army captured Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 景懼，遣泗州牙將王知朗至徐州，稱唐皇帝奉書，願效貢賦，陳兄事之禮，世宗不答。

translations.literal: Jing was afraid; he sent Sizhou staff officer Wang Zhilang to Xuzhou, calling himself the Tang emperor presenting a letter, wishing to render tribute and levies, setting forth the rites of treating Zhou as elder brother; Shizong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Li Jing dispatched Wang Zhilang, a staff officer from Sizhou, to Xuzhou with a letter from the emperor of Southern Tang offering tribute and declaring himself Zhou's younger brother. Shizong ignored him.

sentences.zh: 景東都副留守馮延魯、光州刺史張紹、舒州刺史周祚、泰州刺史方訥皆棄城走；

translations.literal: Jing's eastern capital deputy custodian Feng Yanlu, Guang Prefecture prefect Zhang Shao, Shu Prefecture prefect Zhou Zuo, and Tai Prefecture prefect Fang Ne all abandoned their cities and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanlu, Li Jing's deputy custodian of the eastern capital, along with the prefects Zhang Shao of Guang, Zhou Zuo of Shu, and Fang Ne of Tai, all abandoned their cities and fled;

sentences.zh: 延魯削髮為僧，為周兵所獲。

translations.literal: Yanlu shaved his head to become a monk and was captured by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanlu shaved his head and disguised himself as a monk, but Zhou soldiers captured him anyway.

sentences.zh: 蘄州裨將李福殺其刺史王承雋降周。

translations.literal: Qizhou vice-commander Li Fu killed its prefect Wang Chengjun and surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Qizhou, the deputy commander Li Fu murdered Prefect Wang Chengjun and surrendered the city to the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 景益懼，始改名璟以避周廟諱，遣其翰林學士鐘謨、文理院學士李德明奉表稱臣，獻犒軍牛五百頭、酒二千石、金銀羅綺數千，請割壽、濠、泗、楚、光、海六州，以求罷兵。

translations.literal: Jing grew ever more afraid; he first changed his name to Jing (璟) to avoid the Zhou ancestral taboo, and dispatched his Hanlin academician Zhong Mo and Wenli Academy academician Li Deming to present a memorial declaring himself minister, offering five hundred head of cattle to reward the army, two thousand piculs of wine, and several thousand measures of gold, silver, and silk gauze, requesting to cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai in order to seek cessation of hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's fear deepened. He changed his written name to Jing to avoid the taboo on the Zhou temple name, then sent the Hanlin scholar Zhong Mo and Wenli Academy scholar Li Deming with a memorial acknowledging Zhou overlordship. The embassy brought five hundred oxen, two thousand piculs of wine, and thousands of bolts of gold, silver, and silk brocade as gifts for the army, and offered to surrender the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai if the Zhou would halt their advance.

sentences.zh: 世宗不報，分兵襲下揚、泰。

translations.literal: Shizong did not reply; he divided troops to descend on Yang and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong made no response and instead sent detachments to strike Yangzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 景遣人懷蠟丸書走契丹求救，為邊將所執。

translations.literal: Jing sent men carrying a letter in a wax pill to flee to the Khitan to seek rescue; they were seized by border generals.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing dispatched messengers with dispatches sealed in wax pellets to beg aid from the Khitan, but border Zhou officers intercepted them.

sentences.zh: 光州刺史張承翰降周。

translations.literal: Guang Prefecture prefect Zhang Chenghan surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chenghan, prefect of Guang, surrendered to the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，景又遣司空孫晟、禮部尚書王崇質奉表，辭益卑服，世宗猶不答，前遣鐘謨等並晟、崇質皆留行在。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year, Jing again dispatched Minister of Works Sun Sheng and Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi to present a memorial; the words grew ever more humble and submissive, yet Shizong still did not reply, and the previously sent Zhong Mo and others together with Sheng and Chongzhi were all detained at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of his fourteenth year, Li Jing sent Sun Sheng, his Minister of Works, and Wang Chongzhi, Minister of Rites, with another memorial even more abject than the last. Shizong still would not answer. He detained Zhong Mo's earlier embassy along with Sun and Wang at his field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 而謨等請歸取景表，盡獻江北地，世宗許之，遣崇質、德明等還，始賜景書曰：「自有唐失禦，天步方艱，六紀於茲，瓜分鼎峙。

translations.literal: But Mo and the others requested to return to obtain Jing's memorial, offering to surrender all the lands north of the Yangtze; Shizong granted this, sent Chongzhi, Deming, and others back, and first bestowed on Jing a letter saying: "Since Tang lost the imperial regalia, the steps of Heaven have been difficult; six reign-periods have passed, and the realm has been carved up like a melon with cauldrons standing opposed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo and his colleagues asked to return to Jinling for a formal submission offering all territory north of the Yangtze. Shizong agreed and sent Wang Chongzhi and Li Deming back with an imperial letter that began: "From the day Tang lost the throne, the realm has fallen into turmoil. Sixty years have passed, and the land has been split among rival regimes like flesh from a melon."

sentences.zh: 自為聲教，各擅蒸黎，交結四夷，憑淩上國。

translations.literal: Each has raised its own voice of instruction, each monopolizes the common people, forms alliances with the four barbarians, and relies on force to bully the Central State.
translations.idiomatic: Each state preaches its own doctrine and holds its own subjects, courts barbarian allies, and presses upon the heartland of civilization.

sentences.zh: 華風不競，否運所鐘，凡百有心，敦不興憤？

translations.literal: Chinese wind does not compete; ill fortune is what is fixed upon—of all who have hearts, who does not rise in indignation?
translations.idiomatic: Chinese civilization has lost its vigor in this age of misfortune—what loyal heart could fail to burn with outrage?

sentences.zh: 朕擅一百州之富庶，握三十萬之甲兵，農戰交修，士卒樂用，茍不能恢復內地，申畫邊疆，便議班旋，真同戲劇。

translations.literal: I monopolize the wealth of a hundred prefectures and grasp three hundred thousand armored troops; agriculture and warfare are jointly cultivated, soldiers rejoice to be employed—if I cannot recover the inner lands and extend the mapped frontier, yet discuss withdrawing the army, it would truly be like a play.
translations.idiomatic: With the riches of a hundred prefectures and an army of three hundred thousand men, with farms and forges both flourishing and soldiers eager for battle—if I marched home without recovering our lost heartland and securing our borders, the whole campaign would be nothing but a farce.

sentences.zh: 至於削去尊稱，願輸臣節，孫權事魏，蕭詧奉周，古也雖然，今則不取。

translations.literal: As for cutting away honored titles and wishing to render minister's submission—Sun Quan served Wei, Xiao Cha honored Zhou; in antiquity it was so, yet today I do not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: You offer to renounce your imperial title and submit as a vassal. Sun Quan bowed to Wei; Xiao Cha served the Zhou of old. Such things happened in former ages—but I want no part of them now.

sentences.zh: 但存帝號，何爽歲寒？

translations.literal: Only preserving the imperial title—what harm in the cold of the year?
translations.idiomatic: Merely keeping your imperial title—what does that cost me, any more than the pine survives the winter?

sentences.zh: 倘堅事大之心，必不迫人於險。

translations.literal: If you steadfastly maintain a heart of serving the greater power, I will surely not drive men into peril.
translations.idiomatic: Hold firm to your duty as the lesser state, and I will not push you to extremes.

sentences.zh: 」德明等還，盛稱世宗英武，景不悅。

translations.literal: Deming and the others returned and extravagantly praised Shizong's martial prowess; Jing was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deming and his party returned, they spoke at length of Shizong's martial brilliance. Li Jing took offense.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘、陳覺等皆以割地無益，而德明賣國以圖利。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu, Chen Jue, and others all held that ceding land was of no benefit, and that Deming was selling the state to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu, Chen Jue, and their faction argued that surrendering territory would accomplish nothing and accused Li Deming of betraying the realm for personal gain.

sentences.zh: 景怒，斬德明。

translations.literal: Jing was angry and beheaded Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Li Jing had Li Deming executed.

sentences.zh: 遣元帥齊王景達與陳覺、邊鎬、許文縝率兵趣壽春，景達將朱元等復得舒、蘄、泰三州。

translations.literal: He dispatched the commander-in-chief, Prince of Qi Jingda, together with Chen Jue, Bian Hao, and Xu Wenzhen to lead troops toward Shouchun; Jingda leading Zhu Yuan and others recovered the three prefectures of Shu, Qi, and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing sent his heir apparent, Prince Jingda of Qi, with Chen Jue, Bian Hao, and Xu Wenzhen to march on Shouchun. Under Prince Jingda and Zhu Yuan, Southern Tang forces recaptured Shu, Qi, and Tai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 夏，大雨，周師在揚、滁、和者皆卻，諸將請要其險隘擊之。

translations.literal: In summer, great rain fell; Zhou troops at Yang, Chu, and He all withdrew, and the generals requested to intercept them at narrow passes and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, heavy rains drove the Zhou garrisons at Yangzhou, Chuzhou, and Hezhou to pull back. Southern Tang generals urged an ambush at the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘曰：「擊之怨深，不如縱之以為德。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu said: "Striking them would deepen resentment; it is better to release them and make it a virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu said, "If we attack them now, we will only deepen their hatred. Better to let them go and claim the moral high ground."

sentences.zh: 」誡諸將閉壁，無得要戰，故周師皆集於壽州。

translations.literal: He admonished the generals to shut their walls and not seek decisive battle; thus Zhou troops all gathered at Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the generals to hold their defenses and avoid battle, allowing the entire Zhou army to concentrate at Shouzhou unopposed.

sentences.zh: 世宗屯於渦口，欲再幸揚州，宰相範質以師老泣諫，乃班師，以李重進攻廬、壽，向訓守揚州。

translations.literal: Shizong encamped at Wokou and wished to visit Yangzhou again; Chancellor Fan Zhi, weeping, remonstrated that the army was weary; he then withdrew the army, assigning Li Chongjin to attack Lu and Shou, and Xiang Xun to guard Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong camped at Wokou and prepared to march on Yangzhou again. Chancellor Fan Zhi pleaded through tears that the troops were exhausted, and Shizong agreed to withdraw. He left Li Chongjin to besiege Luzhou and Shouchun while Xiang Xun held Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 訓請棄揚州，並力以攻壽春，乃封府庫付主者，遣景舊將按巡城中，秋毫不犯而去，淮人大悅，皆負糗糧，以送周師。

translations.literal: Xun requested to abandon Yangzhou and combine strength to attack Shouchun; he then sealed the treasury and entrusted it to its custodian, sent Jing's former generals to patrol the city—not violating the slightest thing in departing; the Huai people were greatly pleased and all shouldered dried rations to see off the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun proposed abandoning Yangzhou to concentrate on Shouchun. He sealed the city treasuries, sent Southern Tang veterans to patrol the streets, and withdrew without looting a single item. The people of the Huai region were overjoyed and brought provisions to sustain the Zhou army on its march.

sentences.zh: 十五年，景達遣朱元等屯紫金山，築甬道以餉壽州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Jingda dispatched Zhu Yuan and others to encamp at Purple Gold Mountain and built a supply corridor to provision Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Prince Jingda posted Zhu Yuan and others on Purple Gold Mountain and constructed a fortified supply line to feed Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 二月，世宗復南征，徙下蔡浮橋於渦口，為鎮淮軍，築二城以夾淮。

translations.literal: In the second month, Shizong again marched south; he moved the Xia Cai floating bridge to Wokou, establishing the Zhenhuai Army, and built two cities to flank the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Shizong launched another southern campaign. He moved the floating bridge from Xia Cai to Wokou, established the Zhenhuai garrison, and built twin fortresses flanking the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 周師連破紫金諸寨。

translations.literal: Zhou troops in succession broke the Purple Gold stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army overran the Purple Gold Mountain encampments one after another.

sentences.zh: 景達雖為元帥，兵事皆決於陳覺。

translations.literal: Although Jingda served as commander-in-chief, all military affairs were decided by Chen Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingda held the title of commander, but Chen Jue made every military decision.

sentences.zh: 覺與朱元素有隙，以元李守貞客，反覆難信，景遣大將楊守忠代元，且召之。

translations.literal: Jue had long had a rift with Zhu Yuan; holding that Yuan had been a client of Li Shouzhen and was fickle and hard to trust, Jing dispatched great general Yang Shouzhong to replace Yuan and also summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue bore a grudge against Zhu Yuan and convinced Li Jing that Yuan—once a retainer of the rebel Li Shouzhen—could not be trusted. Li Jing sent Yang Shouzhong to replace him and ordered Zhu Yuan to report to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元憤怒，叛降於周，諸軍皆潰，許文縝、邊鎬皆被執，景達以舟兵奔還金陵。

translations.literal: Yuan was angry and defected to surrender to Zhou; all armies collapsed; Xu Wenzhen and Bian Hao were both captured; Jingda with river troops fled back to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan, furious, defected to the Zhou. The Southern Tang army dissolved. Xu Wenzhen and Bian Hao were taken prisoner, and Prince Jingda fled by river to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 劉仁贍病且死，其副使孫羽等以壽州降於周。

translations.literal: Liu Renshan was ill and near death; his deputy Sun Yu and others surrendered Shouzhou to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renshan lay dying of illness. His deputy Sun Yu and the garrison surrendered Shouchun to the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗班師。

translations.literal: Shizong withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong marched his army home.

sentences.zh: 景遣人焚揚州，驅其士庶而去。

translations.literal: Jing sent men to burn Yangzhou and drove off its gentry and common people.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing ordered Yangzhou burned and its population driven south.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，世宗復南征，遂圍濠州，刺史郭廷謂告於周曰：「臣不能守一州以抗王師，然願請命於唐而後降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Shizong again marched south and thereupon besieged Hao Prefecture; Prefect Guo Tingwei reported to Zhou: "Your minister cannot hold one prefecture to resist the royal army, yet I wish to request orders from Tang and then surrender."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Shizong launched yet another southern campaign and laid siege to Hao Prefecture. Prefect Guo Tingwei sent word to the Zhou: "I cannot hold this prefecture against the imperial army, but I ask permission to receive orders from Southern Tang before I surrender."

sentences.zh: 」世宗為之緩攻，廷謂遣人請命於景，景許其降，乃降。

translations.literal: Shizong for this reason slackened the attack; Tingwei sent men to request orders from Jing; Jing permitted his surrender, and he then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong held his fire. Guo Tingwei sent messengers to Li Jing, received permission to yield, and then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又取泗州。

translations.literal: They also took Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou also captured Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 周師步騎數萬，水陸齊進，軍士作《檀來》之歌，聲聞數十里。

translations.literal: Zhou troops' infantry and cavalry numbered in the tens of thousands; by land and water they advanced together; soldiers composed the song "Tan Lai," and the sound was heard for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Zhou infantry and cavalry advanced by land and river together, soldiers singing the marching air "Tan Lai" loud enough to carry for miles.

sentences.zh: 十二月，屯於楚州之北門。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, they encamped at the north gate of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army encamped at the north gate of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，周師南征，無水戰之具，已而屢敗景兵，獲水戰卒，乃造戰艦數百艘，使降卒教之水戰，命王環將以下淮。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhou troops marched south, they had no equipment for water warfare; before long they repeatedly defeated Jing's soldiers, captured troops skilled in river combat, then built several hundred warships, had surrendered soldiers teach river warfare, and ordered Wang Huan to lead them downstream on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army first marched south it had no fleet. Soon it was beating Li Jing's forces on the water, taking prisoners who knew river fighting, building hundreds of warships, and putting surrendered men to teaching Zhou sailors how to fight on the Huai. Wang Huan was ordered to lead the fleet downstream.

sentences.zh: 景之水軍多敗，長淮之舟，皆為周師所得。

translations.literal: Jing's river forces suffered many defeats; all boats on the Long Huai fell to Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's navy lost battle after battle, and every vessel on the Huai fell into Zhou hands.

sentences.zh: 又造齊雲船數百艘，世宗至楚州北神堰，齊雲舟大，不能過，乃開老鸛河以通之，遂至大江。

translations.literal: They also built several hundred Qiyun ships; when Shizong reached the Beishen Dam at Chuzhou, the Qiyun vessels were too large to pass, so they opened the Laoguan River to channel them through, and thus reached the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: They built hundreds more tower-ships called Qiyun. When Shizong came to the Beishen Dam at Chuzhou the new vessels were too large to pass, so the Laoguan River was cut open to float them through, and the fleet at last reached the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 景初自恃水戰，以周兵非敵，且未能至江。

translations.literal: At first Jing relied on water warfare, believing Zhou troops were no match and could not reach the river.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing had counted on his mastery of river fighting, sure the Zhou army was no match on the water and could never reach the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 及覺奉使，見舟師列於江次甚盛，以為自天而下，乃請曰：「臣願還國取景表，盡獻江北諸州，如約。

translations.literal: When Jue was serving as envoy, he saw the fleet arrayed at the riverbank in great strength and thought it had descended from heaven; he then pleaded: "Your minister wishes to return to his state to obtain Jing's memorial and surrender all prefectures north of the river, as agreed."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jue went as envoy and saw the Zhou fleet massed along the river, he took it for an army fallen from the sky. He begged leave to return home and fetch Li Jing's formal submission, offering every prefecture north of the river as promised.

sentences.zh: 」世宗許之，始賜景書曰「皇帝恭問江南國主」，勞其良苦而已。

translations.literal: Shizong agreed and for the first time sent Jing a letter reading "The Emperor respectfully inquires after the Lord of Jiangnan," merely comforting him for his great toil.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong consented and for the first time wrote to Li Jing, "The Emperor respectfully inquires after the Lord of Jiangnan"—nothing more than a word of sympathy for his ordeal.

sentences.zh: 是時，揚、泰、滁、和、壽、濠、泗、楚、光、海等州，已為周得，景遂獻廬、舒、蘄、黃，畫江以為界。

translations.literal: At this time Yang, Tai, Chu, He, Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, Hai, and other prefectures had already been taken by Zhou; Jing then surrendered Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang, drawing the river as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yangzhou, Taizhou, Chu, Hezhou, Shouzhou, Haozhou, Sizhou, Chuzhou, Guangzhou, Haizhou, and the rest had fallen to the Zhou. Li Jing yielded Luzhou, Shuzhou, Qizhou, and Huangzhou as well, and the Yangtze was fixed as the border.

sentences.zh: 五月，景下令去帝號，稱國主，奉周正朔，時顯德五年也。
