translations.literal: In the fifth month, Jing ordered removal of the imperial title, styled himself Lord of the State, adopted Zhou's calendar and era designation—it was the fifth year of Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Li Jing renounced the imperial title, called himself merely Lord of the State, and adopted the Zhou calendar. It was the fifth year of Xiande.

sentences.zh: 初，孫晟使於周，留不遣，而世宗問晟江南虛實，不對，世宗怒，殺晟。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sun Sheng had been envoy to Zhou and was detained; Shizong questioned Sun Sheng about conditions in Jiangnan, but he would not answer; Shizong was furious and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Sheng had gone as envoy to the Zhou and was held there. Shizong pressed him for intelligence on Jiangnan; Sun Sheng refused to speak. Shizong in anger had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 周已罷兵，景乃贈劉仁贍太師，追封晟魯國公。

translations.literal: After Zhou had ceased hostilities, Jing posthumously honored Liu Renshan as Grand Preceptor and posthumously ennobled Sun Sheng as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Zhou had stood down their armies, Li Jing posthumously honored Liu Renshan as Grand Preceptor and ennobled the dead Sun Sheng as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣鐘謨、馮延魯歸國。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Zhong Mo and Feng Yanlu back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent Zhong Mo and Feng Yanlu home.

sentences.zh: 景復遣謨等朝京師，手自書表，稱天地父母之恩不可報，又請降詔書同藩鎮，遣謨面陳願傳位世子。

translations.literal: Jing again sent Mo and the others to pay court at the capital; he personally wrote the memorial, declaring that the grace of Heaven and Earth and of parents could never be repaid; he also requested an edict treating him like a military governor and sent Mo to state in person his wish to pass the throne to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing sent Mo and his party to the capital again with a memorial in his own hand, protesting that the kindness of Heaven, Earth, and his sovereign parents could never be repaid. He asked to be treated in edicts like any frontier governor and sent Mo to say face to face that he wished to abdicate in favor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣謨等還國，優詔以勞安之。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Mo and the others back to their country with a gracious edict expressing sympathy and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent them home with a warm edict of consolation and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 景以謨為禮部侍郎、延魯戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Jing appointed Mo Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Yanlu Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing made Zhong Mo Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Feng Yanlu Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 景為太子時；

translations.literal: When Jing was crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing was still crown prince,

sentences.zh: 延魯等皆出入東宮，禮部尚書常夢錫自世屢言不可使延魯等近太子，及景立，延魯用事，夢錫每排斥之。

translations.literal: Yanlu and his circle had all frequented the Eastern Palace; Minister of Rites Chang Mengxi had long said from the first that Yanlu and the others must not be allowed near the crown prince; once Jing ascended, Yanlu held power, and Mengxi constantly opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanlu and his friends had come and gone freely in the Eastern Palace. Minister of Rites Chang Mengxi had warned for years that men like Yanlu must be kept away from the heir. When Li Jing took the throne Yanlu rose to power, and Mengxi fought him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 景既割地稱臣，有語及朝廷為大朝者，夢錫大笑曰：「君等嘗欲致君如堯、舜，今日自為小朝邪？

translations.literal: Once Jing had ceded territory and become a vassal, when someone spoke of the court as the Great Court, Mengxi laughed loudly and said: "You once wished to make your lord like Yao and Shun. Are you making yourselves a lesser court today?"
translations.idiomatic: After Li Jing had surrendered territory and bowed as a vassal, someone spoke of the Zhou court as the Great Court. Mengxi burst out laughing. "You once wanted a ruler as sage as Yao or Shun," he said. "And now you call yourselves a lesser court?"

sentences.zh: 」鐘謨素善李德明，既歸，而聞德明由宋齊丘等見殺，欲報其冤，未能發。

translations.literal: Zhong Mo had long been on good terms with Li Deming; after returning, he heard that Deming had been killed through the machinations of Song Qiqiu and others; he wished to vindicate Deming's unjust death but could not find an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo had always been close to Li Deming. Back home he learned that Deming had been killed at the instigation of Song Qiqiu and his faction. He wanted to right that wrong but found no way to act.

sentences.zh: 陳覺，齊丘黨也，與嚴續素有隙。

translations.literal: Chen Jue was of Song Qiqiu's faction and had long had enmity with Yan Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue belonged to Song Qiqiu's clique and had long hated Yan Xu.

sentences.zh: 覺嘗奉使周，還言世宗以江南不即聽命者，嚴續之謀，勸景誅續以謝罪。

translations.literal: When Jue had served as envoy to Zhou, on returning he said that Shizong attributed Jiangnan's failure to promptly obey orders to Yan Xu's schemes and urged Jing to execute Xu to atone.
translations.idiomatic: After a mission to the Zhou, Chen Jue reported that Shizong blamed Jiangnan's delay in submitting on Yan Xu and urged Li Jing to execute Xu as an act of contrition.

sentences.zh: 景疑之，謨因請使於周，驗其事。

translations.literal: Jing was doubtful; Mo therefore requested a mission to Zhou to verify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing was not convinced. Zhong Mo volunteered to go to the Zhou and learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 景已割地稱臣，乃遣謨入朝謝罪，言不即割地者，非續謀，願赦之。

translations.literal: Jing having already ceded land and become a vassal, sent Mo to court to confess guilt, saying that the delay in ceding territory had not been Xu's scheme and asking that Xu be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, who had already surrendered his lands and accepted vassal status, sent Mo to court to plead forgiveness, insisting that the delay in yielding territory had not been Yan Xu's doing and begging that Xu be spared.

sentences.zh: 世宗大驚，曰：「續能為謀，是忠其主也，朕豈殺忠臣乎？

translations.literal: Shizong was greatly astonished and said: "Xu could devise stratagems—that is loyalty to his master. How would I kill a loyal minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was astonished. "If Xu gave counsel," he said, "it was loyalty to his lord. Would I execute a faithful minister?"

sentences.zh: 」謨還，言覺奸詐，景怒，流覺饒州，殺之，宋齊丘坐覺黨與，放還青陽，賜死。

translations.literal: Mo returned and reported that Jue was treacherous and deceitful; Jing was furious, exiled Jue to Raozhou and had him executed; Song Qiqiu was implicated as Jue's accomplice, was sent back to Qingyang, and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo came back he exposed Chen Jue's fraud. Li Jing in fury banished Jue to Raozhou and had him killed. Song Qiqiu, convicted as Jue's accomplice, was sent home to Qingyang and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 以太弟景遂為洪州節度使，燕王冀為太子。

translations.literal: The younger imperial brother Li Jingsui was made military governor of Hongzhou; Prince of Yan Li Ji was made crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's younger brother Li Jingsui was appointed military governor of Hongzhou, and the Prince of Yan, Li Ji, was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 景困於用兵，鐘謨請鑄大錢以一當十，文曰「永通泉貨」。

translations.literal: Jing, pressed by warfare, Zhong Mo requested casting large coins worth ten each, inscribed "Ever-Flowing Currency."
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed by war, Li Jing accepted Zhong Mo's proposal to mint heavy coins worth ten ordinary cash each, bearing the inscription Ever-Flowing Currency.

sentences.zh: 謨嘗得罪，而大錢廢。

translations.literal: Mo once fell from favor, and the large coins were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo later fell from favor the large coins were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 韓熙載又鑄鐵錢，以一當二。

translations.literal: Han Xizai then cast iron coins, each worth two.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai then minted iron coins worth two ordinary cash each.

sentences.zh: 九月，太子冀卒，次子從嘉封吳王，居東宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Crown Prince Ji died; the second son Congjia was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu and installed in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Crown Prince Ji died. The second son, Congjia, was made Prince of Wu and installed in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 鐘謨言從嘉輕肆，請立紀國公從善，景怒，貶謨國子司業，立從嘉為太子。

translations.literal: Zhong Mo said Congjia was frivolous and unrestrained and urged installing Duke of Ji Li Congshan; Jing was angry, demoted Mo to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and installed Congjia as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo called Congjia reckless and urged making Duke of Ji Congshan heir instead. Li Jing was furious, demoted Mo to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and confirmed Congjia as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 世宗使人謂景曰：「吾與江南，大義已定，然慮後世不能容汝，可及吾世修城隍、治要害為子孫計。

translations.literal: Shizong sent someone to tell Jing: "Between me and Jiangnan the grand settlement is fixed, yet I fear later ages will not spare you. While I live you should repair walls and moats and secure key points for your descendants' sake."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent word to Li Jing: "The broad terms between us are settled, but I fear later rulers may not leave you in peace. While I am alive, repair your walls and fortify your strong points—for your children's sake."

sentences.zh: 」景因營緝諸城，謀遷其都於洪州，群臣皆不欲遷，惟樞密使唐鎬贊之，乃升洪州為南昌，建南都。

translations.literal: Jing therefore repaired all the cities and planned to move the capital to Hongzhou; the ministers all opposed relocation; only Privy Council Director Tang Hao approved; Hongzhou was elevated to Nanchang and established as the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing set about repairing every city and planned to move the capital to Hongzhou. The court opposed the move; only Privy Council Director Tang Hao spoke in favor. Hongzhou was renamed Nanchang and made the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，留太子從嘉監國，景遷於南都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, he left Crown Prince Congjia to oversee the state and Jing moved to the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong he left Crown Prince Congjia to govern at home and moved himself to the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 而洪州迫隘，宮府營廨，皆不能容，群臣日夕思歸，景悔怒不已。

translations.literal: But Hongzhou was cramped; palace offices and government buildings could not accommodate them; the ministers day and night longed to return; Jing's remorse and rage never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhou proved cramped. Palaces and government halls could not hold the court. The ministers thought of nothing but going home, and Li Jing brooded in anger and regret.

sentences.zh: 唐鎬慚懼，發疾卒。

translations.literal: Tang Hao, ashamed and afraid, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Hao, shamed and terrified, took ill and died.

sentences.zh: 六月，景卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Jing died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Jing died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 從嘉嗣立，以喪歸金陵，遣使入朝，願復景帝號，太祖皇帝許之，乃謚曰明道崇德文宣孝皇帝，廟號元宗，陵曰順陵。

translations.literal: Congjia succeeded to the throne, brought the coffin back to Jinling, sent envoys to court requesting restoration of Jing's imperial title; Emperor Taizu granted it; he was posthumously titled Emperor Mingdao Chongde Wenxuan Xiao, temple name Yuanzong, tomb name Shunling.
translations.idiomatic: Congjia succeeded him, brought the coffin back to Jinling, and sent envoys asking that Li Jing's imperial title be restored. Emperor Taizu agreed. Li Jing was posthumously styled Emperor Mingdao Chongde Wenxuan Xiao, given the temple name Yuanzong, and buried at Shunling.

sentences.zh: 煜字重光，初名從嘉，景第六子也。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Chongguang, originally named Congjia, was Jing's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, whose courtesy name was Chongguang and who had first been named Congjia, was Li Jing's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 煜為人仁孝，善屬文，工書畫，而豐額駢齒，一目重瞳子。

translations.literal: Yu was benevolent and filial by nature, skilled at literary composition, accomplished in calligraphy and painting, yet had a broad forehead, joined teeth, and a double pupil in one eye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was gentle and filial, wrote well, and excelled at calligraphy and painting. He had a broad forehead, teeth grown close together, and a double pupil in one eye.

sentences.zh: 自太子冀已上，五子皆早亡，煜以次封吳王。

translations.literal: From Crown Prince Ji upward, five sons had all died early; Yu was next in line and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The five sons above him, beginning with Crown Prince Ji, had all died young. Yu was next in line and was made Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，景遷南都，立煜為太子，留監國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, when Jing moved to the Southern Capital, he installed Yu as crown prince and left him to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong, when Li Jing moved to the Southern Capital, he named Yu crown prince and left him to govern at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 景卒，煜嗣立於金陵。

translations.literal: When Jing died, Yu succeeded at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing died, Yu took the throne at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 母鐘氏，父名泰章。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady Zhong; his father was named Taizhang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Zhong; his father was named Taizhang.

sentences.zh: 煜尊母曰聖尊後；

translations.literal: Yu honored his mother as Sage Empress Dowager;
translations.idiomatic: Yu honored his mother as Sage Empress Dowager;

sentences.zh: 立妃周氏為國後；

translations.literal: installed Consort Zhou as empress of the state;
translations.idiomatic: installed Consort Zhou as empress;

sentences.zh: 封弟從善韓王，從益鄭王，從謙宜春王，從度昭平郡公，從信文陽郡公。

translations.literal: enfeoffed younger brothers Congshan as Prince of Han, Congyi as Prince of Zheng, Congqian as Prince of Yichun, Congdu as Marquis of Zhaoping, and Congxin as Marquis of Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed his brothers Congshan as Prince of Han, Congyi as Prince of Zheng, Congqian as Prince of Yichun, Congdu as Marquis of Zhaoping, and Congxin as Marquis of Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 大赦境內。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was declared within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 遣中書侍郎馮延魯修貢於朝廷，令諸司四品已下無職事者，日二員待制於內殿。

translations.literal: He sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Feng Yanlu to present tribute to the court and ordered that officials of the fourth rank and below without active duties should serve two at a time as attendants-in-waiting in the inner hall each day.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Feng Yanlu to the Song court with tribute and ordered that idle officials of the fourth rank and below should attend in the inner hall two at a time each day.

sentences.zh: 三年，泉州留從效卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, Liu Congxiao, military commissioner of Quanzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his reign Liu Congxiao, the military commissioner at Quanzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 景之稱臣於周也，從效亦奉表貢獻於京師，世宗以景故，不納。

translations.literal: When Jing submitted as minister to Zhou, Congxiao also presented a memorial offering tribute to the capital, but Shizong, for Jing's sake, would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing submitted to Zhou as a vassal, Congxiao also sent a memorial with tribute to the capital, but Shizong, out of deference to Jing, refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 從效聞景遷洪州，懼以為襲己，遣其子紹基納貢於金陵，而從效病卒，泉人因並送其族於金陵，推立副使張漢思。

translations.literal: Congxiao heard that Jing was moving to Hong Prefecture and feared he meant to attack him; he sent his son Shaoji to present tribute at Jinling. Congxiao then died of illness, and the people of Quan Prefecture sent his entire clan to Jinling as well and installed the vice commissioner Zhang Hansi as leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Congxiao learned that Li Jing was relocating the capital to Hongzhou, he feared a move against him and sent his son Shaoji with tribute to Jinling. Congxiao then fell ill and died, whereupon the people of Quanzhou dispatched his whole clan to Jinling as well and installed the vice commissioner Zhang Hansi in his place.

sentences.zh: 漢思老不任事，州人陳洪進逐之，自稱留後，煜即以洪進為節度使。

translations.literal: Hansi was old and could not manage affairs. Chen Hongjin of the prefecture drove him out, declared himself acting military commissioner, and Yu immediately made Hongjin military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Hansi was too old to govern. Chen Hongjin of the prefecture expelled him, proclaimed himself acting military commissioner, and Yu at once appointed Hongjin military governor.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，始用鐵錢，民間多藏匿舊錢，舊錢益少，商賈多以十鐵錢易一銅錢出境，官不可禁，煜因下令以一當十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, iron coins were first put into use. The people hoarded old coins in large numbers, so old coins grew ever scarcer. Merchants often exchanged ten iron coins for one copper coin to take out of the realm, and the government could not stop it. Yu therefore ordered that one iron coin should count for ten.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, iron coinage was introduced. People hoarded old coins in large numbers until they grew scarce, and merchants often traded ten iron coins for one copper coin to smuggle across the border. The government could not stop it, so Yu ordered that one iron coin should be worth ten.

sentences.zh: 拜韓熙載中書侍郎、勤政殿學士。

translations.literal: Han Xizai was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician of the Hall of Diligence in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician of the Hall of Diligence in Governance.

sentences.zh: 封長子仲遇清源公，次子仲儀宣城公。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhongyu was enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyuan, and his second son Zhongyi as Duke of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his eldest son Zhongyu as Duke of Qingyuan and his second son Zhongyi as Duke of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 五年，命兩省侍郎、給事中、中書舍人、集賢勤政殿學士，分夕於光政殿宿直，煜引與談論。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he ordered the vice directors of the two secretariats, supervisory censors, drafting counselors of the Secretariat, and academicians of the Hall of Collecting Worthies and the Hall of Diligence in Governance to take turns keeping night watch at the Hall of Glorious Governance, and Yu would summon them for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he ordered vice directors of the two secretariats, supervisory censors, drafting counselors, and academicians of the Collecting Worthies and Diligence in Governance halls to rotate night duty at the Hall of Glorious Governance, and Yu would call them in for conversation.

sentences.zh: 煜嘗以熙載盡忠，能直言，欲用為相，而熙載後房妓妾數十人，多出外舍私侍賓客，煜以此難之，左授熙載右庶子，分司南都。

translations.literal: Yu considered Xizai utterly loyal and able to speak bluntly and wished to make him chief minister, but Xizai kept dozens of singing girls in his rear chambers, many of whom were housed outside to wait on guests in private. Yu found this hard to accept and demoted Xizai to Right Principal of the Heir Apparent, with appointment at the Southern Capital only.
translations.idiomatic: Yu regarded Xizai as utterly loyal and outspoken and wanted to make him chief minister, but Xizai kept dozens of concubines and singing girls, many lodged outside to entertain guests in private. Yu could not stomach it and demoted him to Right Principal of the Heir Apparent, with duties at the Southern Capital only.

sentences.zh: 熙載盡斥諸妓，單車上道，煜喜留之，復其位。

translations.literal: Xizai dismissed all the women and set off alone in a single cart. Yu was pleased and kept him, restoring his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai sent away all the women and set out alone in a single cart. Yu was delighted, kept him at court, and restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 已而諸妓稍稍復還，煜曰：「吾無如之何矣！

translations.literal: Before long the women gradually returned. Yu said, "There is nothing I can do about it!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long the women gradually drifted back. Yu said, "There is nothing I can do about it!"

sentences.zh: 」是歲，熙載卒，煜嘆曰：「吾終不得熙載為相也。

translations.literal: That year Xizai died. Yu sighed and said, "In the end I never had Xizai as chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: That year Xizai died. Yu sighed and said, "In the end I never made Xizai my chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」欲以平章事贈之，問前世有此比否，群臣對曰：「昔劉穆之贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He wished to posthumously grant him the title of Grand Counselor and asked whether any precedent existed from earlier ages. The ministers replied, "In the past Liu Mushi was posthumously granted Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: He wished to posthumously grant him the title of Grand Counselor and asked whether precedent allowed it. The ministers answered, "Liu Mushi was once posthumously granted Commissioner with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 」遂贈熙載平章事。

translations.literal: Accordingly he posthumously granted Xizai the title of Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He then posthumously granted Xizai the title of Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 熙載，北海將家子也，初與李穀相善。

translations.literal: Xizai was the son of a military family from Beihai and had once been on good terms with Li Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai came from a military family in Beihai and had once been close friends with Li Gu.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，熙載南奔吳，穀送至正陽，酒酣臨訣，熙載謂穀曰：「江左用吾為相，當長驅以定中原。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Mingzong, Xizai fled south to Wu. Gu escorted him as far as Zhengyang. As the wine went to their heads at their parting, Xizai said to Gu, "If Jiangzuo appoints me chief minister, I shall drive north at full speed to pacify the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Mingzong's reign, Xizai fled south to Wu. Gu escorted him as far as Zhengyang, and as the wine warmed them at their farewell, Xizai told Gu, "If the south appoints me chief minister, I shall ride north at full speed and pacify the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 」穀曰：「中國用吾為相，取江南如探囊中物爾。

translations.literal: Gu said, "If the Central States appoint me chief minister, taking Jiangnan will be like reaching into a bag and pulling out what is inside."
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied, "If the north appoints me chief minister, taking Jiangnan will be like reaching into a bag and taking what you want."

sentences.zh: 」及周師之征淮也，命穀為將，以取淮南，而熙載不能有所為也。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army campaigned in Huainan, Gu was appointed a general to seize the Huai lands, yet Xizai could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army marched on Huainan, Gu was appointed a general to seize the region — yet Xizai could do nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，煜遣其弟韓王從善朝京師，遂留不遣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, Yu sent his brother Prince Han Congshan to pay court at the capital, and he was detained and not allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao, Yu sent his brother, Prince Han Congshan, to pay court at the capital. He was detained and never sent home.

sentences.zh: 煜手疏求從善還國，太祖皇帝不許。

translations.literal: Yu wrote a personal petition asking that Congshan be sent back to his state, but Emperor Taizu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yu wrote a personal petition begging that Congshan be allowed to return, but Emperor Taizu refused.

sentences.zh: 煜嘗怏怏以國蹙為憂，日與臣下酣宴，愁思悲歌不已。

translations.literal: Yu often brooded unhappily over the shrinking of his realm, drinking deep with his ministers day after day in mournful song that would not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yu brooded constantly over the shrinking of his realm, drinking deep with his ministers day after day in songs of grief that never ended.

sentences.zh: 五年，煜下令貶損制度。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yu ordered a reduction of ceremonial institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Yu ordered a scaling back of court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 下書稱教，改中書、門下省為左、右內史府，尚書省為司會府，御史臺為司憲府，翰林為文館，樞密院為光政院，諸王皆為國公，以尊朝廷。

translations.literal: Edicts were issued as "Instructions." The Secretariat and Chancellery were renamed the Left and Right Directorates of Internal Affairs, the Department of State Affairs became the Directorate of Audits, the Censorate became the Directorate of Law, the Hanlin Academy became the Literary Institute, the Bureau of Military Affairs became the Directorate of Glorious Governance, and all princes were made State Dukes, all to show deference to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts went out as "Instructions." The Secretariat and Chancellery became the Left and Right Directorates of Internal Affairs; the Department of State Affairs, the Directorate of Audits; the Censorate, the Directorate of Law; the Hanlin Academy, the Literary Institute; and the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Directorate of Glorious Governance. All princes were reduced to State Dukes — every change meant to honor the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 煜性驕侈，好聲色，又喜浮圖，為高談，不恤政事。

translations.literal: By nature Yu was proud and extravagant, fond of music and women, devoted to Buddhism, given to lofty talk, and heedless of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was proud and extravagant by nature, devoted to music and women, enamored of Buddhism, fond of lofty talk, and indifferent to the business of rule.

sentences.zh: 六年，內史舍人潘佑上書極諫，煜收下獄，佑自縊死。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Internal Affairs Drafting Counselor Pan You submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance. Yu had him imprisoned, and You hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Internal Affairs Drafting Counselor Pan You submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance. Yu had him thrown into prison, and You hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 七年，太祖皇帝遣使詔煜赴闕，煜稱疾不行，王師南征，煜遣徐鉉、周惟簡等奉表朝廷求緩師，不答。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Emperor Taizu sent envoys summoning Yu to court. Yu claimed illness and did not go. When the imperial army marched south, Yu sent Xu Xuan, Zhou Weijian, and others with a memorial to the court begging a halt to the campaign. No answer came.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Emperor Taizu sent envoys summoning Yu to court. Yu pleaded illness and stayed home. When the imperial army marched south, Yu dispatched Xu Xuan, Zhou Weijian, and others with a memorial begging the court to halt the campaign. No reply came.

sentences.zh: 八年十二月，王師克金陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year, the imperial army captured Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eighth year, the imperial army took Jinling.

sentences.zh: 九年，煜俘至京師，太祖赦之，封煜違命侯，拜左千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Yu was brought captive to the capital. Taizu pardoned him, enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Disobeyed Orders, and appointed him General of the Left Guard of the Thousand-Ox.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Yu was brought captive to the capital. Taizu pardoned him, enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Disobeyed Orders, and appointed him General of the Left Guard of the Thousand-Ox.

sentences.zh: 其後事具國史。

translations.literal: Matters thereafter are recorded fully in the national chronicles.
translations.idiomatic: What happened afterward is set out fully in the national chronicles.

sentences.zh: 予世家江南，其故老多能言李氏時事，云太祖皇帝之出師南征也，煜遣其臣徐鉉朝於京師。

translations.literal: I come from a family long established in Jiangnan. Many old men among us could still speak of affairs in the Li reign. They said that when Emperor Taizu marched south on campaign, Yu dispatched his minister Xu Xuan to pay court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: My family has lived in Jiangnan for generations, and many old men among us could still recount affairs from the Li reign. They said that when Emperor Taizu marched south on campaign, Yu sent his minister Xu Xuan to pay court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 鉉居江南，以名臣自負，其來也，欲以口舌馳說存其國，其日夜計謀思慮言語應對之際詳矣。

translations.literal: Xuan had made his career in Jiangnan and took pride in his reputation as an eminent minister. He came intending to save his state through eloquent persuasion, and he planned and rehearsed his arguments day and night down to the last word of every exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had built his reputation in Jiangnan and took pride in standing among its great ministers. He came intending to save his state through eloquence alone, and he planned and rehearsed his arguments day and night, down to the last word of every exchange.

sentences.zh: 及其將見也，大臣亦先入請，言鉉博學有材辯，宜有以待之。

translations.literal: When the time for his audience drew near, a senior minister went in first and said that Xuan was learned, talented, and skilled in debate, and that he ought to receive a careful welcome.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience drew near, a senior minister went in first and said that Xuan was learned, talented, and skilled in debate, and that he deserved a careful welcome.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑曰：「第去，非爾所知也。

translations.literal: Taizu smiled and said, "Go. This is not for you to understand."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu smiled and said, "Go. This is not for you to understand."

sentences.zh: 」明日，鉉朝於廷，仰而言曰：「李煜無罪，陛下師出無名。

translations.literal: The next day Xuan appeared at court and, looking up, declared, "Li Yu is guilty of nothing. Your Majesty's campaign has no just cause."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xuan appeared at court and, looking up, declared, "Li Yu is guilty of nothing. Your Majesty's campaign has no just cause."

sentences.zh: 」太祖徐召之升，使畢其說。

translations.literal: Taizu slowly beckoned him forward and let him finish his speech.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu slowly beckoned him forward and let him finish.

sentences.zh: 鉉曰：「煜以小事大，如子事父，未有過失，奈何見伐？

translations.literal: Xuan said, "Yu serves the greater power with the deference of a son toward a father. He has committed no offense. Why send troops against him?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "Yu serves the greater power as a son serves a father. He has done no wrong. Why march against him?"

sentences.zh: 」其說累數百言。

translations.literal: His speech ran to several hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: His speech ran to several hundred words.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「爾謂父子者為兩家可乎？

translations.literal: Taizu said, "Do you think father and son can be two separate houses?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Do you think father and son can be two separate houses?"

sentences.zh: 」鉉無以對而退。

translations.literal: Xuan had no reply and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had no answer and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，大哉，何其言之簡也！

translations.literal: Alas — how grand, and how spare his words were!
translations.idiomatic: Alas — how grand, and how spare his words were!

sentences.zh: 蓋王者之興，天下必歸於一統。

translations.literal: When a true king rises, the realm must ultimately be united as one.
translations.idiomatic: When a true king rises, the realm must ultimately be united as one.

sentences.zh: 其可來者來之，不可者伐之；

translations.literal: Those who may come, let them come; those who will not, attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who may come, let them come; those who will not, attack them.

sentences.zh: 僭偽假竊，期於掃蕩一平而後已。

translations.literal: Usurpers, pretenders, and petty thieves — the aim is to sweep them all away and restore peace.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpers, pretenders, and petty thieves — the aim is to sweep them all away and leave the realm at peace.

sentences.zh: 予讀周世宗《征淮南詔》，怪其區區攈摭前事，務較曲直以為辭，何其小也！

translations.literal: When I read Emperor Shizong of Zhou's "Edict on the Huainan Campaign," I marvel that he should rummage through petty old grievances and argue right and wrong as his justification — how cramped!
translations.idiomatic: When I read Emperor Shizong of Zhou's "Edict on the Huainan Campaign," I marvel that he rummages through petty old grievances and argues right and wrong as his justification — how cramped!

sentences.zh: 然世宗之英武有足喜者，豈為其辭者之過歟？

translations.literal: Yet Shizong's martial prowess is surely worth celebrating. Can that be blamed on whoever drafted his words?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shizong's martial prowess is surely worth celebrating. Can that be blamed on whoever drafted his words?

sentences.zh: （據湯悅所撰《江南錄》云：「景以保大十五年正月，改元交泰，是歲盡獻淮南十四州，畫江為界。

translations.literal: (According to Tang Yue's Record of Jiangnan: "In the first month of the fifteenth year of Baoda, Jing changed the reign title to Jiaotai; that same year he surrendered all fourteen Huainan prefectures and drew the Yangtze as the boundary."
translations.idiomatic: (According to Tang Yue's Record of Jiangnan: "In the first month of the fifteenth year of Baoda, Jing changed the reign title to Jiaotai; that same year he surrendered all fourteen Huainan prefectures and drew the Yangtze as the boundary."

sentences.zh: 」保大十五年，乃周顯德四年也。

translations.literal: "Baoda fifteenth year" corresponds to the fourth year of Xiande in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: "Baoda fifteenth year" corresponds to the fourth year of Xiande in Zhou.

sentences.zh: 案《五代舊史》及《世宗實錄》，顯德四年十月壬申，世宗方復南征，五年正月丙午，始克楚州。

translations.literal: But according to the Old History of the Five Dynasties and the Veritable Record of Emperor Shizong, in the fourth year of Xiande, on the day renshen of the tenth month, Shizong had only just renewed the southern campaign; on the day bingwu of the first month of the fifth year he first captured Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: But according to the Old History of the Five Dynasties and the Veritable Record of Emperor Shizong, in the fourth year of Xiande, on the day renshen of the tenth month, Shizong had only just renewed the southern campaign; on the day bingwu of the first month of the fifth year he first captured Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月己亥，景始盡獻淮南諸州，畫江為界，當是保大十六年也。

translations.literal: On the day jihai of the second month, Jing only then surrendered all the Huainan prefectures and drew the Yangtze as boundary — that should be Baoda sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai of the second month, Jing only then surrendered all the Huainan prefectures and drew the Yangtze as the boundary — that should be Baoda sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 悅等南唐故臣，記其目見之事，何其差繆？

translations.literal: Yet Yue and his fellows were former ministers of Southern Tang, recording what they saw with their own eyes — how could they be so far wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yue and his fellows were former ministers of Southern Tang, recording what they saw with their own eyes — how could they be so far wrong?

sentences.zh: 而《九國志》、《紀年通譜》之類，但以悅書為正，不復參校，遂皆差一年。

translations.literal: Works such as the *Record of the Nine States* and the *Comprehensive Chronology* took Yue's book alone as correct and did not cross-check further, and thus all differ by one year.
translations.idiomatic: Texts such as the *Record of the Nine States* and the *Comprehensive Chronology* treated Yue's book as authoritative without further cross-checking, and so they are all off by one year.

sentences.zh: 至於景滅閩國，是保大四年，《江南錄》書於三年，亦差一年，已具《閩世家》註。

translations.literal: As for Jing's destruction of the state of Min, it was in the fourth year of Baoda; the *Record of Jiangnan* places it in the third year, again one year off, as is already set forth in the notes to the *Hereditary House of Min*.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing's destruction of Min fell in the fourth year of Baoda, but the *Record of Jiangnan* dates it to the third year—again a one-year error, already discussed in the notes to the *Hereditary House of Min*.

sentences.zh: 或疑景立逾年而改元，則滅閩國當為三年，周取淮南當為十五年不差，但《江南錄》誤於景立之年改元保大，所以常差一年也。

translations.literal: Some suspect that Jing changed the era name only after more than a year on the throne, in which case destroying Min should be the third year and the Zhou seizure of Huainan the fifteenth year without error; but the *Record of Jiangnan* wrongly changed the era to Baoda in the year Jing was enthroned, and therefore is constantly one year off.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that Jing changed the era name only after his second year on the throne, which would make the fall of Min year three and the Zhou conquest of Huainan year fifteen without discrepancy. But the *Record of Jiangnan* wrongly proclaimed the Baoda era in the very year of his accession, which is why it is habitually one year behind.

sentences.zh: 今知不然者，以諸書參校，閩人殺王延羲，當晉開運元年，周師始伐南唐當顯德二年。

translations.literal: That this is not so is now known by cross-checking various books: the men of Min killed Wang Yanxi in what should be the first year of Kaiyun of Jin, and the Zhou army first attacked Southern Tang in what should be the second year of Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-checking other sources shows this theory is wrong: the murder of Wang Yanxi by the Min faction belongs in the first year of Jin's Kaiyun era, and the Zhou opening of hostilities against Southern Tang belongs in the second year of Xiande.

sentences.zh: 據景以初立之年即改元，則開運元年為保大二年，顯德二年為保大十三年。

translations.literal: According to Jing's changing the era name in the very year of his first enthronement, the first year of Kaiyun would be the second year of Baoda, and the second year of Xiande the thirteenth year of Baoda.
translations.idiomatic: If Jing did change the era in his accession year, then Kaiyun 1 equals Baoda 2 and Xiande 2 equals Baoda 13.

sentences.zh: 今《江南錄》書延羲被殺於二年，周師始伐於十三年，則是景立之年改元，不誤，而悅等書滅王氏、割淮南自各差一年爾。

translations.literal: Now the *Record of Jiangnan* places Yanxi's killing in the second year and the Zhou army's first attack in the thirteenth year; thus Jing's changing the era in his enthronement year is not in error, and it is Yue and his fellows' accounts of destroying the Wang clan and ceding Huainan that each differ by one year.
translations.idiomatic: The *Record of Jiangnan* dates Yanxi's death to year 2 and the Zhou invasion to year 13, which confirms that Jing's accession-year era change is correct. Yue and his colleagues are the ones who are each one year off in dating the fall of the Wang house and the cession of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 自晉天福二年建國，至皇朝開寶八年國滅，凡三十九年。）〉

translations.literal: From establishing the state in the second year of Tianfu of Jin to the state's destruction in the eighth year of Kaibao of the August Dynasty, altogether thirty-nine years.)〉
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the state in Jin Tianfu 2 to its fall in our dynasty's Kaibao 8, the realm lasted thirty-nine years in all.)
